pol.next_election: General election on November 7, 2026 (early voting began October 26)

GBR.leader: Prime Minister Andy Burnham (Labour; took office July 20, 2026) / King Charles III
GBR.situation: After a rout in the May local elections, Starmer announced his resignation on June 22, and Burnham won the Labour leadership contest in July to become Britain's seventh prime minister in a decade. Abroad, London is keeping up support for Ukraine (including handing over Storm Shadow design data) and its target of defense spending at 3.5 percent of GDP, but gilt yields have climbed to their highest since 2008, sharply reducing fiscal headroom. In the fallout from the Iran war, the bases at Akrotiri in Cyprus and Diego Garcia came under attack, and in August Iran-linked hackers shut down a power plant for four days.

mil.note: A nuclear power, Britain has decided to rejoin NATO nuclear sharing by acquiring 12 F-35As. The gap between what the Ministry of Defence requests and what the Treasury allocates remains wide, however.

pol.regime: Constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary system
pol.stability: Labour's parliamentary majority is solid, but its poll numbers have collapsed, and the surge of Reform UK is increasing pressure for a change of government.
pol.next_election: The next general election must be held by August 2029 at the latest

econ.note: Soaring energy prices and rising gilt yields are estimated to have cut fiscal headroom to about £8 billion, making the October 28 budget a test.

recent.text: Prime Minister Starmer announced his resignation after the local election rout and mounting pressure within the party.
Andy Burnham, winner of the Labour leadership contest, took office as prime minister and appointed John Healey chancellor of the exchequer.
Prime Minister Burnham said he would keep the pledge to raise defense spending and create 500,000 defense and aerospace jobs by 2030.

Gilt yields rose to their highest since the 2008 financial crisis, and analysts estimated that fiscal headroom had been cut in half.

Whether the Hormuz maritime mission that Britain agreed to lead jointly with France actually gets under way
Whether the crackdown on Russia's shadow fleet and Iranian cyber retaliation spill over into security on British soil
uncertain: Details of 2026 policy changes on AUKUS could not be confirmed (reports say it is proceeding). Whether a Quad leaders' summit will be held this year is undecided.

FRA.leader: President Emmanuel Macron / Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu (reappointed October 10, 2025)
FRA.situation: In a parliament with no majority, Prime Minister Lecornu is hanging on, surviving one no-confidence threat after another. Ahead of the 2027 presidential election, the National Rally (RN) leads in the polls. In March, Macron announced an increase in nuclear warheads and a plan for extended deterrence across Europe, and France agreed to lead a Hormuz maritime mission with Britain, though the mission has stalled. Having missed its 2026 deficit target, the government has proposed €54 billion in spending cuts.

mil.note: The EU's only nuclear power; in March 2026 it announced an increase in warheads and the Europeanization of nuclear deterrence (talks with Germany and Britain).

pol.stability: A minority government faces a no-confidence threat with every budget and, with the presidential election approaching, is squeezed from both the far right and the far left.
pol.next_election: Presidential election: first round April 18, 2027; runoff May 2, 2027

econ.note: The government has pledged €54 billion in cuts to bring the 2027 deficit down to 5 percent of GDP, but with the Middle East pushing up fuel prices and interest costs rising, it is unclear whether the plan will pass.

recent.text: The French navy seized the Russian shadow-fleet tanker Deliver near Sicily, its fifth boarding since September 2025.
An appeals court shortened Marine Le Pen's ban from public office, clearing the way for her to run in the 2027 presidential election.
France said it would soon launch a maritime security mission in the Strait of Hormuz with Britain, but actual deployment had been delayed as of August.
Prime Minister Lecornu acknowledged that the 2026 deficit target would be missed and unveiled the outline of a €54 billion austerity budget for 2027.

watch: Whether a no-confidence motion passes during October's budget debate and brings down the government
The shape of the 2027 presidential race, especially whether the RN candidate is Le Pen or Jordan Bardella, and whether the center unites behind one candidate
Whether Europeanizing nuclear deterrence leads to actual deployments or agreements with Germany and others
uncertain: Active-duty IISS troop numbers are taken from a Wikipedia table (mixing the 2024–2026 IISS editions): Britain 141,100 / France 203,900 / Germany 179,850 / Poland 173,000. They have not been cross-checked against the original Military Balance 2026. Poland's Defense Ministry says it has more than 220,000 active personnel.

The figure of 370 French nuclear warheads is the total inventory, including retired warheads awaiting dismantlement, in a table in the summary of the SIPRI Yearbook 2026. SIPRI puts France's military stockpile at 290, the same as in the 2025 edition. Because France stopped disclosing its stockpile in March 2026, both figures are SIPRI estimates.

DEU.leader: Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU) / President Frank-Walter Steinmeier
DEU.situation: With military spending of $114 billion in 2025, Germany ranked fourth in the world, and by stationing a permanent armored brigade in Lithuania it has become the center of European rearmament. In September's state elections, the AfD took 43.8 percent in Saxony-Anhalt; in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, the AfD came first and the CDU fell below 5 percent; and in Berlin, the Left Party finished first. These were the worst results ever for parties in government, and they have badly sapped the momentum of Merz's coalition. Berlin formally blamed Russia for an incident involving explosive-laden drones at Leipzig airport, stepping up its response to Russian hybrid warfare.

mil.note: The world's fourth-largest military spender by SIPRI's count. Germany has no nuclear weapons but takes part in NATO nuclear sharing (U.S. B61 bombs) and is a party to talks on French nuclear deterrence.

pol.stability: The CDU-SPD coalition is holding, but the AfD is at or near the top of national polls at around 30 percent, and there is a risk that forming governments in the eastern states will become paralyzed.
pol.next_election: Bundestag elections in 2029 (regular schedule). The Federal Convention will elect the next federal president on January 30, 2027

econ.note: Europe's largest economy, but stagnation persists: manufacturing is losing more than 10,000 jobs a month, and the economy is vulnerable to energy price shocks.

recent.text: Germany signed a bilateral defense cooperation agreement with Poland.
Germany for the first time formally blamed Russia for an incident involving explosive-laden drones near Leipzig/Halle airport. Russia retaliated by closing the Goethe-Institut.
In the Saxony-Anhalt state election, the AfD won a landslide 43.8 percent but fell short of a majority. The CDU managed only 17.2 percent.

The AfD came first in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, where the CDU failed to clear the 5 percent threshold, and in Berlin the Left Party finished first for the first time. Merz acknowledged the results as a disaster but declared that the coalition would continue.

watch: Whether the firewall against the AfD holds as governments are formed in Saxony-Anhalt and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania
The Merz coalition's reform agenda and pressure on the SPD to walk away
How quickly the Lithuania brigade reaches full strength, and the spread of Russian hybrid attacks (drones, sabotage)
uncertain: IISS active-duty troop numbers are taken from a Wikipedia compilation (mixing the IISS 2024–2026 editions): U.K. 141,100 / France 203,900 / Germany 179,850 / Poland 173,000. They could not be cross-checked against the original Military Balance 2026. Poland's defense ministry has said it has more than 220,000 active-duty troops.
The Federal Convention that elects Germany's next federal president will meet on January 30, 2027 (set by the Bundestag president on February 26, 2026); Steinmeier's term ends on March 18, 2027.

POL.leader: President Karol Nawrocki (PiS-aligned) / Prime Minister Donald Tusk (Civic Coalition)
POL.situation: A frontline state on NATO's eastern flank, Poland put 4.7 percent of GDP into defense in 2025 and 5 percent in 2026 and is building Europe's largest land army. In July, a Russian cruise missile came down near Lublin, and in September a Mi-8 helicopter from Kaliningrad violated its airspace; such provocations have become routine. At home, the cohabitation clash between President Nawrocki and the Tusk government has deepened, leading to a presidential veto of EU defense loans (SAFE) and a push for constitutional change.

mil.note: At 4.7 to 5 percent of GDP, its defense spending is the highest share in NATO. The defense ministry says active-duty personnel exceed 220,000 (a figure that differs from the IISS count).

pol.regime: Parliamentary system (directly elected president with veto power)
pol.stability: A cohabitation arrangement pits the president against the government. Veto politics is paralyzing legislation, and the right-wing opposition is regrouping.
pol.next_election: Parliamentary elections, fall 2027

econ.note: Among the fastest-growing large EU economies; rising defense spending is propping up growth while adding to the fiscal burden.

recent.text: Poland signed a bilateral defense cooperation agreement with Germany.

President Nawrocki stripped Zelensky of the Order of the White Eagle after the Ukrainian president decorated a unit that claims the legacy of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA), straining relations with Ukraine.
A cruise missile believed to be Russian came down near Lublin, and NATO fighter jets were scrambled.
Nawrocki launched a constitutional commission to strengthen presidential powers; the Tusk government declined to take part.
A Russian Mi-8 helicopter from Kaliningrad violated Polish airspace for 42 seconds, and Poland expanded its air defenses in the east.

watch: Whether Russian missile, drone, and helicopter incursions lead to discussions under NATO's Article 4 or Article 5
Whether Nawrocki's vetoes continue to block defense procurement (including SAFE) and judicial reform
The regrouping of the right-wing opposition ahead of the 2027 elections, and the Tusk coalition's poll numbers
uncertain: IISS active-duty troop numbers are taken from a Wikipedia compilation (mixing the IISS 2024–2026 editions): U.K. 141,100 / France 203,900 / Germany 179,850 / Poland 173,000. They could not be cross-checked against the original Military Balance 2026. Poland's defense ministry has said it has more than 220,000 active-duty troops.

ITA.leader: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni / President Sergio Mattarella
ITA.situation: The Meloni government is stable, having set the record as the longest-serving cabinet since World War II, but a budget deficit stuck at 3.1 percent has dashed hopes of exiting the EU's excessive deficit procedure, and ahead of the 2027 election it faces pressure from rivals further to the right.

recent.text: The Meloni cabinet became the longest-serving Italian government since World War II.
Italian Air Force fighters shot down a drone that had entered Lithuanian airspace (as part of NATO's Baltic Air Policing mission).

mil.note: Military expenditure in 2025 was 1.9 percent of GDP, according to SIPRI. Under the Defense Ministry's multiyear plan (2025–2027), the ministry's ordinary budget is €31.298 billion in 2025 (up 7.2 percent from the previous year), €31.209 billion in 2026 and €31.749 billion in 2027. For 2025, Italy reported to NATO a figure of 2 percent of GDP, which includes accounting reclassification.

pol.regime: Parliamentary republic (the president is elected by a joint session of parliament)
pol.next_election: General election in 2027 (the current parliament's term ends in autumn 2027)
pol.stability: In September 2026 the Meloni government became Italy's longest-serving government of the postwar era. On October 8 the Chamber of Deputies passed a new electoral law that the government had tied to confidence votes, and the opposition has questioned its constitutionality.

watch: The Constitutional Court's ruling on the new electoral law, and the timing of the general election
The path of the defense budget toward NATO's Hague target (3.5 percent plus 1.5 percent of GDP within 10 years, with a review in 2029). The 2026 ordinary budget is slightly lower than in 2025
Whether the EU excessive deficit procedure is lifted (deficit at 3.1 percent)

ESP.leader: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez / King Felipe VI
ESP.situation: The Sánchez government is shaken by corruption scandals and a minority position in parliament but is holding on. Spain is the NATO member most reluctant to embrace the 5 percent target, yet its economy is growing faster than any other large eurozone economy.

recent.text: During the UN General Assembly, Prime Minister Sánchez publicly criticized the Trump administration, continuing his confrontational line toward Washington.
Spanish F-18s scrambled after detecting an aerial target over Ukraine near the Romanian border (a NATO eastern-flank mission).
Prime Minister Sánchez dissolved parliament and called an early general election for November 29.

mil.note: Military expenditure in 2025 was 2.1 percent of GDP, according to SIPRI.

uncertain: The item in Spain's recent developments on criticism of the United States at the UN General Assembly was confirmed only at the level of a headline.

pol.regime: Constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary system
pol.next_election: Early general election on November 29, 2026 (called by Prime Minister Sánchez on October 5)

NLD.leader: Prime Minister Rob Jetten (D66, took office February 23, 2026) / King Willem-Alexander
NLD.situation: A three-party minority cabinet of D66, the VVD and the CDA took office without a confidence-and-supply agreement with the opposition, the first such case since 1918, leaving an unstable arrangement that must find a fresh majority for every bill. As host of the NATO summit in The Hague, the Netherlands maintains its line on deterring Russia and raising defense spending.

recent.text: The Jetten cabinet (a D66-VVD-CDA minority coalition) took office.

mil.note: Military expenditure in 2025 was 2.2 percent of GDP, according to SIPRI.

pol.regime: Constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary system
pol.next_election: House of Representatives election by 2030 at the latest (regular date not yet set)

SWE.leader: Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson (outgoing, caretaker) → new parliament opened September 28; vote on Magdalena Andersson as prime minister after September 29 / King Carl XVI Gustaf
SWE.situation: In the September 13 election, the left-wing bloc won narrowly, 176 seats to 173, and Prime Minister Kristersson announced his resignation; parliament could vote on a new prime minister as early as September 29. Conflict with the Center Party over bringing the Left Party into government makes coalition-building shaky, but the defense course set since NATO accession is expected to keep cross-party support.

recent.text: The Social Democrats became the largest party, and the left-wing bloc won a majority (176 seats).
Prime Minister Kristersson announced his resignation. Parliament's vote on a prime minister could come as early as September 29.

Sweden's new parliament opened on September 28 and elected a speaker; because the speaker can nominate a candidate for prime minister only after September 29, the vote on Andersson has not yet taken place (left-wing bloc 176 seats, right-wing bloc 173).

mil.note: Military expenditure in 2025 was 2.5 percent of GDP, according to SIPRI.

uncertain: Sweden's next prime minister will be confirmed by a parliamentary vote after September 29. Andersson is the favorite, but the question of the Left Party joining the government could cause delays.

pol.regime: Constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary system
pol.next_election: Parliamentary election in September 2030 (regular, four-year term)

FIN.leader: President Alexander Stubb / Prime Minister Petteri Orpo
FIN.situation: Finland has finished building about 200 kilometers of fence and sensors along its 1,340-kilometer border with Russia and is preparing for the Russian buildup near that border. In the spring, Ukrainian drones knocked off course by Russian electronic warfare strayed into Finnish airspace. Finland is a key frontline state on the Baltic and Arctic fronts.

recent.text: Warnings emerged that Russia is redeploying large forces (up to about 100,000 troops) toward the Finnish border.
The trial of the captain of the Fitburg, in the case of damage to undersea cables in the Gulf of Finland, opened at the Helsinki District Court.

mil.note: Military expenditure in 2025 was 2.6 percent of GDP, according to SIPRI.

pol.next_election: Parliamentary election in April 2027 (regular)

NOR.leader: Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre / King Harald V
NOR.situation: Since the closure of Hormuz, Norway has gained weight as a key energy supplier to Europe. It is NATO's northern front line, facing Russia's Northern Fleet in the Arctic and the Barents Sea.

recent.text: Støre attended the European Arctic summit in Rovaniemi, where leaders discussed linking Arctic and Baltic security.

mil.note: Military expenditure in 2025 was 3.3 percent of GDP, according to SIPRI.

pol.regime: Constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary system
pol.next_election: Parliamentary election in September 2029 (regular; there is no mechanism for dissolving parliament)

ROU.leader: President Nicușor Dan / interim Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan; confirmation vote pending on Prime Minister-designate Siegfried Mureșan (around September 29–30; about 170 seats secured, 233 needed)
ROU.situation: After the Bolojan cabinet fell to a no-confidence vote in May over austerity disputes, Prime Minister-designate Mureșan faces a confirmation vote with a minority coalition of the PNL, USR, and UDMR (170 seats, against the 233 needed for confirmation), and passage is uncertain. Along the Black Sea and Danube borders, Russian drone incursions continue, and Romania shot down a drone on September 24.

recent.text: The Bolojan government fell in a no-confidence vote (281 in favor).
Romanian forces shot down a drone suspected to be Russian.

Prime Minister-designate Mureșan submitted his three-party PNL-USR-UDMR cabinet list and governing program to parliament, but with about 170 seats secured, he is 63 short of the 233 needed for confirmation; the vote will be held at a joint session of both chambers on September 30, and the outcome is uncertain.

uncertain: Romania's confirmation vote on the Mureșan cabinet is expected around September 30; with 170 seats against the 233 needed, passage is uncertain. If it fails, the interim Bolojan arrangement will continue.

HUN.leader: Prime Minister Péter Magyar (Tisza; took office May 9, 2026) / President Tamás Sulyok
HUN.situation: In the April general election, Tisza won 141 of 199 seats, a two-thirds supermajority, ending Orbán's 16 years in power. Hungary has swung to a pro-EU course, recovering EU funds that had been frozen and lifting its veto on EU support for Ukraine.

recent.text: Péter Magyar took office as prime minister, ending the Orbán era.
With Hungary's veto lifted, the EU approved €6.6 billion in military aid to Ukraine through the European Peace Facility (EPF), which had been blocked since 2023.

uncertain: Military spending is not listed for Hungary, Serbia, or the three Baltic states because they do not appear among SIPRI's top 40 countries for 2025.
It could not be verified whether Hungary's president (Tamás Sulyok) remains in office after the Magyar government took power. Magyar's camp has called for his resignation.

mil.note: Military expenditure in 2025 was 2.0 percent of GDP, according to SIPRI.

pol.next_election: Parliamentary election in April or May 2030 (regular)

GRC.leader: Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis / President Konstantinos Tasoulas
GRC.situation: Tensions with Turkey in the Aegean and the eastern Mediterranean have flared again, and Mitsotakis visited Kastellorizo, declaring that Greece takes orders from no one on defense and sovereignty. Defense cooperation with Israel is also provoking Ankara.

recent.text: Mitsotakis warned Turkey that Greece does not take orders on matters of defense and sovereignty.
Mitsotakis visited the island of Kastellorizo, off the Turkish coast, sending a message to Ankara.

mil.note: Military expenditure in 2025 was 3.0 percent of GDP, according to SIPRI.

pol.next_election: Parliamentary election in 2027, when the term ends. Prime Minister Mitsotakis has ruled out an early election

SRB.leader: Acting President Ana Brnabić (speaker of the National Assembly, since September 27, 2026); Prime Minister Đuro Macut. Aleksandar Vučić is running for prime minister in the October 25 snap parliamentary election
SRB.situation: After nearly two years of antigovernment protests that followed the 2024 collapse of a canopy at the Novi Sad railway station, Vučić called a snap parliamentary election for October 25. He has given up the presidency to run for prime minister, aiming to shift his power base. The youth-led protest movement is formally taking part in the election.

recent.text: Vučić called a snap parliamentary election for October 25.

Serbian President Vučić resigned to run for prime minister in the October 25 snap election, and his ally Ana Brnabić, the speaker of the National Assembly, became acting president; just before stepping down, he pardoned 49 people, including 23 jailed in connection with the protests.

Vučić said the first round of a presidential election must be held before the end of the year under the constitution's 90-day deadline; analysts see a close race in the October 25 parliamentary election between the ruling Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) and the student-led movement's list (Students Are Winning).

uncertain: Hungary, Serbia and the three Baltic states are not on SIPRI's 2025 list of the top 40 spenders, so no military spending figure is given.

EST.leader: Prime Minister Kristen Michal / President Alar Karis (President-elect Ülle Madise takes office October 12)
EST.situation: Estonia, a frontline state whose border runs through Narva, saw a Russian drone strike the Auvere power plant in March; in May, a stray drone was shot down in its airspace. On September 2, parliament elected Ülle Madise as the next president.

recent.text: Parliament elected Ülle Madise president (she takes office October 12).
A Romanian F-16 shot down a stray drone over Estonia.

uncertain: Estonia's presidency passes from Karis to Madise on October 12. The results of Latvia's parliamentary election (October 3) and Bosnia's general election (October 4) are not yet in.

mil.note: Military expenditure in 2025 was 3.4 percent of GDP, according to SIPRI.

pol.next_election: Parliamentary election on March 7, 2027 (regular)

LVA.leader: Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs (United List, took office May 2026) / President Edgars Rinkevics
LVA.situation: Latvia heads into an October 3 election in which Kulbergs's United List holds the lead. In response to migration pressure, sabotage and airspace violations by Russia and Belarus, NATO sent additional German Eurofighters for the election period.

recent.text: Two drones that had strayed off course entered Latvia, and one of them exploded at an oil storage facility.
Elections to the Saeima (parliament) are scheduled for October 3.
Prime Minister Kulbergs's United List came first in the general election with 35.3 percent of the vote (97 percent of ballots counted; 42 of 100 seats).

uncertain: Estonia's presidency passes from Karis to Madise on October 12. The results of Latvia's election (October 3) and Bosnia's election (October 4) are not yet known.

mil.note: Military expenditure in 2025 was 3.6 percent of GDP, according to SIPRI.

pol.next_election: Parliamentary election in October 2030 (regular)

LTU.leader: Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius (Social Democrat, confirmed June 30, 2026) / President Gitanas Nausėda
LTU.situation: A frontline state bordering the Suwałki corridor between Belarus and Kaliningrad, Lithuania hosts a permanent German armored brigade (about 4,800 troops). On September 15, NATO fighter jets shot down a drone that had entered from the direction of Belarus. In June, Prime Minister Inga Ruginienė resigned, making her successor the third Social Democratic prime minister since the 2024 election.

recent.text: Parliament confirmed Sinkevičius as prime minister, following Ruginienė's resignation.
NATO (Italian) fighter jets shot down a drone that had entered from the direction of Belarus over eastern Lithuania.

mil.note: Military expenditure in 2025 was 3.1 percent of GDP, according to SIPRI.

pol.next_election: Parliamentary election in October 2028 (regular). Presidential election in May 2029

CZE.leader: Prime Minister Andrej Babiš (ANO) / President Petr Pavel
CZE.situation: The Babiš government is continuing the Czech-led initiative to procure artillery shells for Ukraine but has cut off state financing for it. It is at odds with the pro-Western President Pavel, and the head of Czech intelligence has warned that a Russian attack on Europe could come within months rather than years.

recent.text: The head of Czech intelligence warned that a Russian attack on Europe could come within months.

mil.note: Military expenditure in 2025 was 1.8 percent of GDP, according to SIPRI.

pol.next_election: Chamber of Deputies election in October 2029 (regular). Presidential election in January 2028

DNK.leader: Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen (third term; appointed June 3, 2026) / King Frederik X
DNK.situation: In the snap election in March, the Social Democrats posted their lowest vote share since 1903, but Frederiksen won a third term at the head of a four-party minority coalition. The crisis sparked early in the year by U.S. pressure to annex Greenland was settled, for now, by the U.S.-Denmark-Greenland security agreement of September 22. Washington gained an expansion of Pituffik Space Base and two new bases, and non-NATO countries may not base forces in Greenland without the consent of the parties to the agreement.

recent.text: A Russian corvette fired flares at a Danish navy helicopter near Gedser in the Baltic Sea.
The U.S.-Denmark-Greenland security agreement was signed at the UN General Assembly. It allows the expansion of Pituffik and new bases at Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig, and it has no expiration date.

mil.note: Military expenditure in 2025 was 3.3 percent of GDP, according to SIPRI.

pol.regime: Constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary system
pol.next_election: Parliamentary election by March 2030 at the latest (four years after the early election of March 24, 2026)

CAN.leader: Prime Minister Mark Carney (Liberal; won an outright majority through by-elections in April 2026)
CAN.situation: After trade talks with the United States broke down in late August, Canada answered the 50 percent U.S. tariff by imposing about $20 billion in retaliatory tariffs on September 8, entering a full-scale trade war. Having secured a majority in April, the Carney government stands on a stable domestic footing, but national unity faces a test ahead of the October 19 Alberta referendum on separation.

mil.note: By SIPRI's count, military spending rose 23 percent in 2025 from the previous year to 1.6 percent of GDP, 16th in the world

pol.stability: As a majority government, it has a stable base in Parliament, but the trade war with the United States and Alberta separatism weigh on it
pol.next_election: Federal election before October 2029 (Alberta referendum October 19, 2026)

econ.note: Because about three-quarters of exports go to the United States, a prolonged tariff war would hit manufacturing and agriculture hard

recent.text: At the USMCA joint review, the United States declined to extend the agreement for 16 years, shifting it to annual reviews through 2036

Trade talks with the United States collapsed, and Carney said the U.S. proposal set unfair terms that would have constrained even Quebec's cultural protections and Canada's ability to sign its own free trade agreements
Carney rebutted criticism from Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and said Canada would resume talks when the United States is ready
Canada imposed retaliatory tariffs of 15 to 50 percent on about $20 billion worth of U.S. goods across some 700 product lines, including steel, home appliances, farm machinery, and dairy products

The same day, the United States hit back by banning imports of Canadian dairy products, motorcycles, and alcoholic beverages (effective September 29), excluding Canada from federal procurement, and threatening to block sales by Bombardier

watch: Whether talks resume before or after the U.S. import ban takes effect on September 29
The result of the October 19 Alberta referendum (on a question to begin the separation process)
Whether the annual USMCA reviews and a bilateral U.S.-Mexico deal leave Canada isolated

MEX.situation: Since the killing of CJNG boss "El Mencho" in February, the Sheinbaum government has eased U.S. pressure for military intervention through a hard-line security policy and extraditions to the United States. Washington has refused to extend the USMCA and is maintaining tariffs of 50 percent on steel and aluminum and 25 percent on non-originating autos; the two countries resume trade negotiations in Washington on September 28.

mil.note: Military spending jumped 71 percent in 2024, then fell by a third in 2025; folding the National Guard into the military has enlarged the armed forces

pol.stability: The ruling party's dominance gives the government a firm base, but cartel violence and sovereignty disputes with Washington are ever present
pol.next_election: Federal midterm elections, June 2027 (presidential election in 2030)

econ.note: With exports overwhelmingly dependent on the U.S. market, the annual USMCA review and product-specific tariffs are the biggest variables for growth

recent.text: Washington's refusal to extend the USMCA for 16 years triggered a regime of annual reviews; Mexico said it supports an extension
U.S. forces shot down three cartel drones near the border with a laser weapon
After her 22nd call with Trump, Sheinbaum said a trade deal was making progress, and talks were set to resume in Washington on September 28
Mexico stayed out of the U.S.-led anti-cartel coalition, the Shield of the Americas, but its major cartels are among the 24 groups on the coalition's list of narco-terrorist organizations

watch: Whether steel and auto tariffs come down at the September 28 trade talks in Washington
The possibility of unilateral U.S. strikes on cartels on Mexican soil
The CJNG succession struggle after El Mencho's death and deteriorating security
uncertain: Mexico's figure of 301,000 active-duty troops is an IISS number cited by Wikipedia; whether it includes the absorbed National Guard could not be confirmed in the original source

BRA.leader: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (Workers' Party)
BRA.situation: Ahead of the October 4 first round of the presidential election, Lula, seeking a fourth term, and Flávio Bolsonaro, son of the imprisoned former president Jair Bolsonaro, are locked in a statistical tie in hypothetical runoff polling (47 percent to 45 percent). When Washington imposed 25 percent Section 301 tariffs in July, Lula hit back in the name of defending sovereignty and has held firm in refusing to join the U.S.-led Shield of the Americas.

mil.note: Investment in naval technology development and rising personnel costs lifted military spending 13 percent in 2025, making Brazil the largest spender in South America

pol.stability: A polarized, neck-and-neck presidential race, compounded by infighting on the Supreme Federal Court (STF) and the Banco Master scandal, makes for high uncertainty
pol.next_election: Presidential and general elections: first round October 4, 2026; runoff October 25, 2026 (inauguration January 1, 2027)

econ.note: Modest growth is expected amid U.S. Section 301 tariffs (beef, coffee and aircraft parts exempted) and high interest rates

recent.text: The United States announced 25 percent tariffs on a wide range of Brazilian goods under Section 301 of the Trade Act (effective July 22); Brazil responded with its reciprocity law and a WTO complaint
Lula launched his campaign for a fourth term, putting national sovereignty front and center
In a call of about 80 minutes with Trump, Lula asked to reopen tariff negotiations
The release of messages between Justice Alexandre de Moraes and banker Daniel Vorcaro fueled conflict and investigations within the Supreme Court

Ahead of Brazil's October 4 first-round vote, a Datafolha poll (September 22–23) put Lula at 40 percent and Flávio Bolsonaro at 36 percent, with a hypothetical runoff at 47 to 45 percent, within the margin of error. At the UN on September 23, Lula said that Brazil is no one's backyard.

watch: Vote shares in the October 4 first round and whether a runoff is held on October 25
Post-election instability, including refusal to accept the result and conflict with the judiciary
Negotiations over U.S. Section 301 tariffs and allegations of election interference

VEN.leader: Acting President Delcy Rodríguez (sworn in January 5, 2026; recognized by the United States as head of state in March)
VEN.situation: With Nicolás Maduro, captured in a U.S. military operation on January 3, awaiting trial in New York, the Rodríguez transitional government is cooperating with Washington and has opened up the oil sector, signing an oil agreement in late August covering 65 billion barrels of reserves. Twin earthquakes of magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 on June 24 caused heavy loss of life. No election timetable has been set, and the UN notes that the machinery of repression remains intact.

mil.note: There is no SIPRI estimate because Venezuela has not disclosed military spending for years; Defense Minister Vladimir Padrino López was replaced in March

pol.regime: Transitional authoritarian regime (led by remnants of chavismo, under U.S. patronage)
pol.stability: Outwardly stabilized under U.S. patronage, but fragile given its lack of legitimacy, the unsettled election timetable and earthquake damage
pol.next_election: Presidential election date not set (government–opposition negotiations under way)

econ.note: Sanctions relief and the U.S. oil agreement are expected to revive oil output, but earthquake recovery is a heavy burden

recent.text: A U.S. airstrike (reported June 12–13) killed Tren de Aragua leader "Niño Guerrero" in Bolívar state
Twin earthquakes of magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 struck the Yaracuy area, killing thousands and leaving tens of thousands missing
Under U.S. sponsorship, the government (represented by Jorge Rodríguez) and the opposition (Dinorah Figuera) began negotiating a path to elections, with María Corina Machado excluded
Trump announced an agreement giving the United States a stake in 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil reserves
In her first UN speech, Rodríguez pledged to hold elections, and she met Trump in New York

After a second round of U.S.-backed government–opposition talks, Delcy Rodríguez's transitional government released 39 political prisoners; the same day, rallies in Caracas and elsewhere demanded Machado's safe return and a presidential election.

watch: Whether a presidential election date is set, and Machado's return and candidacy
Implementation of the U.S. oil agreement and the pace of the recovery in output
Whether the machinery of repression, including the military and the colectivos, is dismantled, and Maduro's trial
uncertain: Venezuela earthquake death toll: estimates vary widely—Wikipedia lists 1,719+ (with some 46,000 missing), while ABC News (September 23) reported more than 6,500—so the recent developments section says "thousands."
Venezuela's GDP of $99.7 billion and 2026 growth of 4.0 percent are IMF DataMapper figures; statistics during the transition are of low reliability
Venezuela's military spending is left blank because it is not reported to SIPRI
The exact date of the Caribbean strike that killed four people (reported September 20; the strike itself probably on the 19th) and the cumulative death toll (230+) are estimates

flashpoints.status_ko: In the fifth year of full-scale war, Russia is pressing its offensive toward Kostiantynivka and Dobropillia while Ukraine mounts local counterattacks around Kupiansk, Chasiv Yar, and elsewhere. Every short truce—at Easter in April, on Victory Day in May, and on September 5–8—ended with a return to fighting. Washington is trying to reconvene three-way U.S.-Russia-Ukraine technical talks in the UAE, but Moscow is holding to its demand for all of the Donetsk region.

last_major_event.text: A Russian glide-bomb attack on Zaporizhzhia killed at least 20 people; it followed a nationwide strike on October 7 (at least 28 killed) and an attack on a bus in Kramatorsk on October 8 (33 killed).

flashpoints.name_ko: Iran war and the Strait of Hormuz
flashpoints.status_ko: The war that began with U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28, 2026, is now in its seventh month. After an April ceasefire and a June 17 memorandum of understanding effectively collapsed on July 8, the United States reimposed its naval blockade. In Hormuz, Iran is trying to control passage by attacking merchant ships and laying mines, while the U.S. military escorts transits; U.S. Central Command said on September 25 that it had turned back 122 merchant vessels since the blockade began. Ship-tracking data and U.S. government statements diverge sharply on how much traffic is getting through. Ship-tracking data in early September showed between five and 12 vessels a day, roughly 10 percent of the peacetime level of about 100. Yet U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said on September 28 that about 13 million barrels a day were passing through, and the ship-tracking firm Kpler counted 19 tankers transiting in the week to September 27. On September 25, Iran put forward a roadmap for reopening the strait within seven days, but President Trump rejected it on September 26. On the nuclear front, Natanz and other sites have been destroyed again, but about 440 kilograms of uranium enriched to 60 percent has been beyond IAEA verification since June 2025.

last_major_event.text: Iran called the U.S. reply "insufficient" and said it would not open the strait until its conditions are met; the same day, a tanker was hit by a drone at Oman's Sohar anchorage.

flashpoints.status_ko: The Israel-Hezbollah war, which reignited in March alongside the Iran war, has left Israeli forces occupying about 55 villages south of the Litani River, and fighting continues under a nominal ceasefire. In Gaza, an agreement on the phased disarmament of Hamas was announced on July 31, but whether Israel will formally accept and implement it remains unclear.

last_major_event.text: The Board of Peace announced an agreement on the phased disarmament of Hamas and a phased Israeli withdrawal.

flashpoints.status_ko: The peace treaty initialed at the White House in August 2025 remains unsigned because Armenia has not first amended its constitution, as Azerbaijan demands. Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan's ruling party won the June parliamentary elections but fell short of the seats needed to change the constitution. Construction has yet to begin on the 43-kilometer Meghri section of the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP), for which only about $400 million in initial U.S. funding has been secured, while Turkey and Azerbaijan are pursuing a parallel Kars-Dilucu railway that bypasses Armenia.

last_major_event.text: Pashinyan's ruling party won Armenia's parliamentary elections but fell short of the majority needed to amend the constitution.

flashpoints.status_ko: Under Ahmed al-Sharaa's transitional government, Syria has entered a phase of integration and reconstruction: in August the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) disbanded and merged into the government army, and the United States lifted Syria's designation as a state sponsor of terrorism. Tensions persist, however, as Israel keeps troops in the south and in August struck as far afield as an air base in Idlib. Much depends on whether U.S.-mediated de-escalation talks between Israel and Syria bear fruit.

last_major_event.text: The dissolution of the SDF and its integration into the Syrian army were announced.

flashpoints.status_ko: Ukraine is repeatedly striking Novorossiysk, the Black Sea Fleet's new base, and tankers of Russia's shadow fleet with drones, Neptune missiles, and uncrewed surface vessels. The fleet has effectively been pushed out of Sevastopol, and with even Russia's crude export ports now within Ukraine's reach, the risks to Russian seaborne logistics have grown.

last_major_event.text: Two merchant ships came under drone attack in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone and one sank; the day before, a grain ship had also sunk off Romania.

flashpoints.status_ko: Since the Justice Mission-2025 encirclement drills in December 2025, no named large-scale exercise by the People's Liberation Army (PLA) had been confirmed through September 2026, and Chinese military aircraft entered Taiwan's air defense identification zone (ADIZ) 125 times in August, less than half the monthly average for 2024–25. Gray-zone pressure, however, has become routine, from coast guard incursions around Kinmen and Dongsha (Pratas) to the announced integration of Kinmen and Xiamen. Amid U.S.-China summitry, Trump has treated arms sales to Taiwan as a bargaining chip and Taiwan's Legislative Yuan has cut the defense budget, eroding the political foundations of deterrence.

last_major_event.text: The PLA's Justice Mission-2025 exercise (December 29–30) rehearsed encircling Taiwan, including a port blockade and live fire.

flashpoints.status_ko: At its Ninth Party Congress, North Korea designated South Korea a permanently hostile state and severed inter-Korean links, and its ballistic missile launches have surged in 2026 to nine rounds involving 15 or more missiles. Trump, pursuing a meeting with Kim Jong Un before the end of the year, unilaterally scaled back the joint South Korea-U.S. Ulchi Freedom Shield (UFS) exercise. Seoul has floated a plan to trade a nuclear freeze for sanctions relief, but Pyongyang rejects denuclearization as an agenda item altogether. The expanding deployment of North Korean troops to Russia, now including drone operators, is fueling concern that Moscow will pay Pyongyang back with military technology.

last_major_event.text: North Korea's Foreign Ministry called the Joint Chiefs of Staff's final finding on the mine (October 5) a "self-staged farce" and restated its official position of not discussing military matters with South Korea.

flashpoints.status_ko: For 11 months since Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's remarks on a Taiwan contingency in November 2025, China has maintained a ban on exports of dual-use items and rare earths to Japan, a halt to imports of Japanese seafood, and curbs on travel to Japan. Military pressure has continued as well—fire-control radar lock-ons by fighter jets, live-fire drills near Okinotori, and joint Chinese-Russian bomber flights—and leader-level channels are effectively frozen. Japan is responding by building up its defenses and deepening cooperation with Australia and other partners.

last_major_event.text: China's Commerce Ministry announced a total ban on exports to Japan of dual-use items with military applications, including rare earths.

flashpoints.status_ko: After spending a record number of days in the waters contiguous to the Senkakus in 2025, the China Coast Guard has continued to enter the islands' territorial waters repeatedly in 2026. On June 10 and July 7, the two countries' coast guards faced off in territorial waters around Japanese fishing boats, sharpening a contest over who enforces the law there. A deliberate armed clash is unlikely, but the risk of an accidental one is ever present.

last_major_event.text: Chinese and Japanese coast guard vessels faced off around a Japanese fishing boat in Senkaku territorial waters, and the Japan Coast Guard drove the Chinese ships away.

flashpoints.name_ko: Structures in the Korea-China Provisional Measures Zone (PMZ), Yellow Sea
flashpoints.status_ko: South Korea and China have been at odds over the aquaculture facilities (Shenlan 1 and 2) and a management platform that China installed in the PMZ. After the January summit in Beijing between Lee Jae-myung and Xi Jinping, China moved and dismantled the management platform, which the South Korean government called "meaningful progress." But the aquaculture facilities and many observation buoys remain, and cases of the China Coast Guard obstructing South Korean ocean surveys have piled up, so concerns about gray-zone encroachment have not been laid to rest.

last_major_event.text: After the South Korea-China summit, China began moving and dismantling its management platform in the PMZ.

flashpoints.status_ko: The China Coast Guard maintains a constant presence and blocks Philippine vessels, and buoys and floating platforms apparently installed by China were spotted in late May 2026, heightening fears that artificial structures will go up on the shoal. Standoffs resumed in July right after Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi warned of bitter consequences, and in late September a Philippine-led multinational exercise was held nearby.

last_major_event.text: The China Coast Guard said it had expelled two Philippine vessels from waters near Scarborough Shoal.

flashpoints.status_ko: Since a provisional arrangement in July 2024, Philippine resupply missions to the BRP Sierra Madre had proceeded without interference. On September 24, 2026, however, China Coast Guard vessels and three navy ships obstructed a resupply mission 60 nautical miles from the shoal, forcing it to be called off. The October 21 resupply went through without being blocked, and the China Coast Guard announced that it had taken place "with China's permission." The Philippine military countered that it had not sought permission.

last_major_event.text: Chinese navy and coast guard ships stopped a Philippine resupply mission 60 nautical miles short of the shoal, forcing it to abort.

flashpoints.status_ko: New construction, including what appears to be a radar installation, has been spotted in the Paracels, which China has controlled since 1974, prompting a formal protest from Vietnam in August. Vietnam is also expanding land reclamation in the Spratlys, and the two countries are now competing to fortify the islands.

last_major_event.text: Vietnam's Foreign Ministry demanded that China immediately halt its new construction in the Paracels.

flashpoints.name_ko: India-Pakistan (Kashmir, the Arabian Sea, and the Indus)
flashpoints.status_ko: The ceasefire that ended the four-day conflict of May 2025 is holding, but India continues to hold the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance. In late August the Court of Arbitration constituted under the treaty ruled the suspension invalid, but India does not recognize the court's jurisdiction. On September 15, warships from the two countries collided in the Arabian Sea—their first direct military contact since 2025—and with no naval hotline or incidents-at-sea agreement between them, the risk of accidental escalation is high.

last_major_event.text: An Indian destroyer and a Pakistani patrol vessel, PNS Hunain, collided in the Arabian Sea.

flashpoints.status_ko: Relations have been stabilizing since the 2024 agreement on troop disengagement in eastern Ladakh, and the 25th round of Special Representatives talks in August 2026 discussed which parts of the boundary delimitation could be settled first (an "early harvest"). At a meeting on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in New Delhi in September, Modi and Xi agreed to pursue a fair settlement of the border, but both sides' large troop deployments and China's dam on the upper Brahmaputra remain unresolved.

last_major_event.text: At their summit, Modi and Xi agreed to pursue a fair and reasonable settlement of the border dispute.

flashpoints.status_ko: After clashes in July and December 2025, a ceasefire was reached in a joint statement on December 27 and is holding, but both Thailand and Cambodia call it fragile. Tensions persist over Thailand's cancellation in May of the 2001 memorandum of understanding on maritime boundaries, Cambodia's launch of UN conciliation proceedings in June, and the return of residents to the Ban Nong Chan area, and in September the Thai military warned of a full-scale response.

last_major_event.text: The Thai military warned that it would respond with full force to any Cambodian attack.

flashpoints.status_ko: Min Aung Hlaing became president in April 2026 following elections, but the move is seen as having changed only the outward form of military rule. The junta has regained some of the initiative through conscription and Chinese support, and northern Shan State has stabilized under Chinese-brokered ceasefires, but fighting continues on the Kachin (Bhamo), Rakhine (Sittwe), and Karen fronts.

last_major_event.text: The Kachin Independence Army repelled a junta attempt to break through around Bhamo, and the Arakan Army captured several outposts around Sittwe (according to resistance forces).

flashpoints.status_ko: Since Pakistan declared open war on the Taliban government on February 27, 2026, airstrikes and border clashes have recurred, and a March airstrike on a hospital in Kabul killed more than 260 civilians. Mediation by Qatar, Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and China has failed to produce a lasting ceasefire, and on September 24 Pakistan extended its airstrikes as far as Kandahar, citing a terrorist attack on a police headquarters and drone attacks launched from Afghanistan.

last_major_event.text: Pakistan carried out airstrikes in Afghanistan's Kunar and Helmand provinces; the UN Assistance Mission in Afghanistan said at least 10 civilians were killed, most of them children.

flashpoints.status_ko: With traffic through Hormuz effectively paralyzed by the Iran war, the Strait of Malacca has become even more important strategically to Asia's energy supply chains. In April, Indonesia's finance minister floated the idea of charging transit fees, then dropped it after the Foreign Ministry objected, but the remark alone pushed up shipping insurance premiums. Piracy and armed robbery incidents in the strait are among the most numerous in Asia.

last_major_event.text: Shipping insurance premiums rose after Indonesia's finance minister floated, then withdrew, the idea of a Malacca transit fee.

flashpoints.name_ko: Baltic Sea, Kaliningrad, and the Suwałki Gap
flashpoints.status_ko: Russian provocations on NATO's eastern flank have multiplied since the start of September. A Russian warship fired flares at a Danish helicopter (September 14), NATO shot down a drone over Lithuania (September 15), and an Mi-8 helicopter from Kaliningrad violated Polish airspace (September 23–24). Lithuania's communications regulator said in May 2026 that GPS-spoofing antennas in Kaliningrad had grown from three in early 2025 to 36, able to spoof signals within a radius of 450 kilometers. Courtroom and maritime standoffs over severed undersea cables and the crackdown on the shadow fleet also continue.

last_major_event.text: In a diplomatic note to NATO member states, Russia claimed that NATO was preparing to blockade Kaliningrad and warned that, in the event of a blockade, it could use all weapons, including nuclear ones.

flashpoints.name_ko: NATO's southeastern airspace (Romania and the Black Sea)
flashpoints.status_ko: Whenever Russia strikes southern Ukraine, drones and missiles stray across Romania's Danube border. On September 24, Romania shot down a drone suspected of being Russian, and on September 25 F-16s and Spanish F-18s were scrambled. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk disclosed intelligence that Russia is planning hybrid drone and missile attacks against countries that support Ukraine.

last_major_event.text: Romanian forces shot down a drone suspected of being Russian.

flashpoints.status_ko: The Greenland crisis, set off by Trump's threats of annexation, was brought into an institutional framework on September 22, when the United States, Denmark, and Greenland concluded a security agreement. Washington gained an expansion of Pituffik and two new bases, a right of consent over any base established by a non-NATO country, and the power to screen foreign investment. Because the agreement remains in force even if Greenland becomes independent, some observers conclude that it has established de facto U.S. security sovereignty over Greenland. The risk of armed conflict has receded, but the sovereignty dispute lies dormant.

last_major_event.text: The United States, Denmark, and Greenland signed an open-ended security agreement (expanding bases and excluding non-NATO countries).

flashpoints.status_ko: In Serbia, after nearly two years of antigovernment protests, Aleksandar Vučić has given up the presidency to run for prime minister in early elections on October 25, aiming to move the center of power to the premiership. In Bosnia, the October 4 general election puts Republika Srpska's separatist course after Milorad Dodik to the test. The question of Serbs in northern Kosovo also remains unresolved, and tensions could rise over this cycle of elections.

last_major_event.text: Vučić resigned as Serbia's president to run for prime minister in the October 25 elections.

flashpoints.name_ko: Russian and Iranian hybrid attacks (Germany and the U.K.)
flashpoints.status_ko: After explosive-laden drones, apparently targeting transport aircraft bound for Ukraine, were found near Leipzig/Halle Airport in August, Germany on September 1 formally named Russia as the culprit for the first time. Britain summoned Russian diplomats, and it emerged that Iran-linked hackers had knocked a British power plant offline for four days. At sea, retaliation for the crackdown on the shadow fleet continues, including a Russian warship firing warning shots at a British yacht.

last_major_event.text: The German government formally attributed the explosive drone incident at Leipzig airport to Russia.

flashpoints.name_ko: Regime change in Venezuela under U.S. pressure
flashpoints.status_ko: After U.S. forces captured Nicolás Maduro on January 3, Washington recognized Delcy Rodríguez's interim government and set up an arrangement under which it effectively oversees Venezuela's oil sector. Armed conflict has subsided, but no election timetable has been set, the apparatus of repression remains in place, and the damage from a major earthquake in June has compounded matters, leaving the transition unstable.

last_major_event.text: Acting President Rodríguez promised elections in a speech at the UN and met with Trump in New York.

flashpoints.name_ko: Strikes on drug boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific (Operation Southern Spear)
flashpoints.status_ko: U.S. military strikes on vessels suspected of carrying drugs, which began in September 2025, have continued for more than a year, and the cumulative death toll has passed 230. The campaign has expanded to strikes on land in Venezuela and Ecuador, and because the United States has not released its evidence, it continues to draw charges of extrajudicial killing.

last_major_event.text: A U.S. strike on a suspected drug boat in the Caribbean killed four people.

flashpoints.status_ko: Since January the United States has been intercepting tankers bound for Cuba and threatening tariffs on countries that supply it with fuel, plunging the island into a humanitarian crisis marked by fuel shortages, the collapse of the power grid, and rising infant mortality. The Trump administration has named Cuba as the next target for regime change and keeps adding sanctions, while talks between the two countries drag on without result.

last_major_event.text: Trump said in his UN speech that freedom is coming to Cuba; Miguel Díaz-Canel hit back, demanding an end to the blockade.

flashpoints.status_ko: Trump has vowed land strikes on the cartels, but no U.S. military strike on Mexican territory has been confirmed to date, and Mexico has eased the pressure for U.S. military intervention by killing El Mencho and carrying out large-scale extraditions. The border is being militarized, with U.S. forces shooting down cartel drones with lasers, and Mexico has stayed out of the Shield of the Americas.

last_major_event.text: U.S. forces used a laser weapon to shoot down three cartel drones near the border.

flashpoints.status_ko: After Panama's Supreme Court in January struck down as unconstitutional CK Hutchison's concession to operate the ports of Balboa and Cristóbal, Denmark's Maersk and MSC took over interim operations. China retaliated with inspections of Panama-flagged ships and stricter customs checks on agricultural products, and the sale of CK Hutchison's ports business to a BlackRock consortium is held up by a Chinese antitrust review.

last_major_event.text: China is reportedly seeking the extradition of a Chinese businessman tied to the ports dispute, and Panama must decide by early November.

flashpoints.status_ko: With the Transitional Presidential Council dissolved in February, Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé governs alone, while gangs control most of Port-au-Prince and about 1.5 million people are internally displaced. The UN-authorized Gang Suppression Force (GSF) has deployed only about 1,000 of its authorized 5,550 personnel, and a vote on extending its mandate looms ahead of its September 30 expiry. On December 13, Haiti is scheduled to hold its first elections since 2016.

last_major_event.text: The Gang Suppression Force announced its first large-scale deployment outside Port-au-Prince, to the Artibonite department.

flashpoints.status_ko: After talks broke down in late August, the United States imposed 50 percent tariffs and Canada retaliated with tariffs on about $20 billion worth of goods, turning the dispute into an all-out trade war between allies. Washington escalated with a ban on imports of Canadian dairy products and alcohol (effective September 29) and exclusion from government procurement, and an October 19 referendum related to Alberta's separation adds to the tension.

last_major_event.text: As Canada's retaliatory tariffs took effect, the United States hit back the same day with an import ban and exclusion from procurement.

flashpoints.name_ko: Ecuador: gang violence and joint operations with U.S. forces
flashpoints.status_ko: With the homicide rate at about 49 per 100,000 people, President Daniel Noboa's government again declared a 60-day state of emergency in September. Since March it has conducted ground strikes alongside the U.S. military near the Colombian border, drawing controversy over errant strikes, while a proposal to allow foreign military bases was rejected in a 2025 referendum.

last_major_event.text: Noboa declared a 60-day state of emergency in eight provinces and a nighttime curfew in four.

flashpoints.status_ko: Since the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) captured El Fasher in October 2025, the front has shifted to Kordofan, where El Obeid is under siege, and to Blue Nile. The war is spilling across borders: the army has struck RSF convoys inside Chad with drones, and RSF drones are alleged to be launching from Ethiopian territory. Five-way mediation by the AU, the EU, IGAD, the Arab League, and the UN has made no progress.

last_major_event.text: The army used drones to strike a convoy of about 200 RSF vehicles near Mourdi, Chad, destroying dozens of them.

flashpoints.name_ko: Sahel jihadist insurgency (Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger)
flashpoints.status_ko: JNIM has been blockading fuel supply routes into Mali's capital, Bamako, for a year, and in April a joint offensive by JNIM and the Azawad Liberation Front (FLA) drove government forces and Russia's Africa Corps out of the north. In Niger, an attempted coup on August 29 was put down with Russian and Algerian support, while mutual assistance within the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) failed to work.

last_major_event.text: JNIM attacked a military base at Dioura, Mali, killing 120 to 150 soldiers.

flashpoints.name_ko: Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (M23 and Rwanda)
flashpoints.status_ko: After M23 seized Goma and Bukavu in 2025, the Washington Accords (DRC-Rwanda) and the Doha Framework (DRC-M23) followed, but implementation has been slow. Despite an August negotiating roadmap and the deployment of ceasefire monitors, government-aligned forces launched offensives toward Minembwe and Walungu, and an Ebola outbreak has deepened the humanitarian crisis.

last_major_event.text: The Washington Accords' Joint Security Coordination Mechanism reconvened in Geneva to review implementation of the commitments on the FDLR and on Rwanda's defensive measures.

flashpoints.name_ko: Horn of Africa (Tigray war and Ethiopia-Eritrea)
flashpoints.status_ko: On September 22, full-scale war broke out in Tigray, Amhara, and Afar between Ethiopian government forces and an antigovernment coalition including the TPLF and Fano militias, effectively bringing down the order established by the Pretoria agreement. The Ethiopian government accuses Eritrea of aiding the rebels, and that charge, coupled with Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's demand for an outlet to the Red Sea (the port of Assab), has raised the risk of war between Ethiopia and Eritrea.

last_major_event.text: Ethiopia's foreign minister sent a letter calling the entry of Eritrean troops a "full-scale invasion" (Eritrea denies it).

flashpoints.name_ko: Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb (Houthis and Yemen's civil war)
flashpoints.status_ko: Alongside the Iran war, the Houthis have stepped up attacks aimed at Saudi Arabia, and with Yemen's civil war reignited they have seized the port of Mocha and Perim Island. The Houthis say they will target only Saudi vessels, but the risks to shipping through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait have grown, and Saudi Arabia's crude export route, rerouted to the Red Sea to avoid Hormuz, is under threat as well.

last_major_event.text: Riyadh's King Khalid Airport was hit, killing 12 people and injuring 309, according to Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority; the Saudi-led coalition launched a large-scale operation against the Houthis on the night of October 9 and claimed to have destroyed 136 targets.

flashpoints.status_ko: With the Hormuz blockade diverting Saudi crude through the East-West Pipeline to the Red Sea, and ships heading north through Suez to escape the Houthi threat, the canal's traffic and toll revenue have rebounded. Transits reached 1,340 in July, up 27 percent from a year earlier, and 2026 revenue is projected at $5.8 billion to $6 billion. Egyptian ports themselves have come under threat, however, as the drone attack on the port of Damietta showed.

last_major_event.text: Suez Canal revenue for July reportedly reached $505 million, the highest since December 2023.

flashpoints.status_ko: Amid the standoff between the Government of National Unity in Tripoli and Khalifa Haftar's forces in the east, a UN-brokered roadmap for unified elections within 24 months was signed on August 30. It needs the approval of the House of Representatives and the High Council of State within a month, and sources of instability remain, including the assassination of the Libyan National Army (LNA) intelligence chief in August and a drone attack on the Zawiya refinery.

last_major_event.text: The rival factions signed a UN-brokered agreement to hold presidential and parliamentary elections within 24 months.

flashpoints.status_ko: When Israel recognized Somaliland in December 2025, Somalia reacted in January 2026 by cancelling all its agreements with the UAE. Armed clashes have broken out in Mogadishu over the extension of President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's term, while Puntland and Jubaland are moving to break away and al-Shabaab is expanding its reach.

last_major_event.text: U.S. Africa Command (AFRICOM) carried out airstrikes against al-Shabaab.

flashpoints.name_ko: U.S.-China chip rivalry and Korean fabs in China
flashpoints.status_ko: At the end of 2025, the United States revoked the validated end-user (VEU) status of Samsung's Xi'an plant and SK hynix's plants in Wuxi and Dalian, issuing equipment import licenses valid only for 2026. The licenses prohibit expansion and upgrades, but the process transitions the two companies carried out around the time the licenses were issued—236-layer NAND at Xi'an and DDR5 at Wuxi—could become a point of contention when the licenses come up for renewal for 2027. With State Council Decree No. 835 (April 2026), China created a legal basis for sanctioning companies that comply with U.S. controls. The U.S.-China summit in September extended the tariff truce to January 10, 2027, but chip controls were not on the agenda.

last_major_event.text: The U.S.-China summit extended the tariff truce to January 10, 2027; chip export controls were left off the agenda.

forecasts.q: A full ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, signed by both sides, takes effect
forecasts.basis: All three short-term ceasefires of 2026 ended in renewed fighting, and Russia has not softened its demand that Ukraine hand over the rest of Donetsk Oblast still under Ukrainian control.
forecasts.s: Full Russia-Ukraine ceasefire takes effect
forecasts.rs: Announcements by the Russian and Ukrainian presidential offices that the ceasefire has been signed and taken effect

forecasts.q: Trilateral technical-level talks among the United States, Russia, and Ukraine actually take place (at any venue)
forecasts.basis: On September 25, Russia and Ukraine agreed to trilateral talks with the United States, but neither the venue (the UAE has been mentioned) nor the agenda has been settled, and Russia launched a large-scale drone attack the same day.
forecasts.s: U.S.-Russia-Ukraine technical talks held
forecasts.rs: Announcements by the White House, the U.S. State Department, the Russian Foreign Ministry or the Office of the President of Ukraine that the talks took place, or Reuters/AP reporting

forecasts.q: A U.S.-Iran ceasefire takes effect and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz is officially announced
forecasts.basis: On September 25, Iran put forward a roadmap for reopening the strait within seven days, but Trump rejected it. There are also reports of a U.S. plan to resume airstrikes after the November midterm elections.
forecasts.s: U.S.-Iran ceasefire and Hormuz reopening
forecasts.rs: Ceasefire announcements by the White House and the Iranian government, and an official announcement on reopening the strait by the Iranian government or U.S. Central Command

forecasts.q: The United States officially announces the resumption of large-scale airstrikes on mainland Iran
forecasts.basis: The case for: Trump's September 23 threat to annihilate Iran and reports of plans to resume bombing after the midterms. The case against: oil prices hovering around $100 a barrel and the room for negotiation after the election.
forecasts.s: U.S. resumes strikes on mainland Iran
forecasts.rs: An official announcement by the White House or the U.S. Department of Defense

forecasts.q: Trump and Kim Jong Un hold a summit
forecasts.basis: Trump has said he wants a meeting this year and has scaled back the Ulchi Freedom Shield (UFS) exercise, but North Korea rejects denuclearization as an agenda item, calling it unrealistic.
forecasts.s: Trump-Kim summit
forecasts.rs: A White House announcement or a KCNA report

forecasts.q: North Korea conducts its seventh nuclear test
forecasts.basis: North Korea has sharply stepped up its missile launches, but having restored relations with both of its patrons, China and Russia, it would pay a high price for a nuclear test at this point.
forecasts.s: North Korea's seventh nuclear test
forecasts.rs: A KCNA announcement, or statements by the South Korean, U.S. or Japanese governments or the CTBTO

forecasts.q: China conducts a named, large-scale joint exercise encircling Taiwan
forecasts.basis: There has been no named large-scale exercise since December 2025, and U.S.-China summit diplomacy is under way. Triggers could include Taiwan's National Day address in October.
forecasts.s: Chinese encirclement drill around Taiwan
forecasts.rs: An announcement by the PLA Eastern Theater Command (including the exercise name)

forecasts.q: A new incident in which China blocks a resupply mission to Second Thomas Shoal is publicly reported
forecasts.basis: Chinese navy and coast guard vessels blocked a Philippine resupply mission on September 24, but the October 21 mission was not blocked. The China Coast Guard announced that it had taken place "with China's permission"; the Philippine military countered that it had not sought permission. If China demands a verification procedure at the next resupply and the Philippines refuses, the mission could be blocked again.
forecasts.s: Second Thomas Shoal resupply blocked again
forecasts.rs: Statements by the Philippine Coast Guard or the Philippine National Maritime Council, or Reuters/AP reporting

forecasts.q: Indian and Pakistani forces engage in interstate fighting that causes casualties
forecasts.basis: Warships of the two countries collided in the Arabian Sea on September 15, but both sides avoided escalation. A major terrorist attack would sharply raise the probability of fighting.
forecasts.s: India-Pakistan military clash
forecasts.rs: Statements by the Indian or Pakistani government or military, or Reuters/AP reporting

forecasts.q: Pakistan and the Afghan Taliban agree to a formal ceasefire
forecasts.basis: Mediation by Qatar, Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and China has failed to produce a lasting ceasefire, and airstrikes on Kandahar in late September raised tensions again.
forecasts.s: Formal Pakistan-Taliban ceasefire
forecasts.rs: Announcements by the Pakistani government and the Taliban government, or by a mediating government

forecasts.q: The U.S.-China tariff truce is extended again before it expires or is replaced by a comprehensive agreement
forecasts.basis: Reciprocal state visits by the U.S. and Chinese leaders in May and September established a framework of strategic stability, and Xi Jinping has said the two should meet again soon. The U.S. Russia sanctions law (the Graham Act), which took effect on September 18, mandates tariffs from October 18 on major buyers of Russian oil and gas and could have collided with the U.S.-China truce had China been targeted, but President Trump waived those tariffs on October 16. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the president would review the effects for up to 60 days.
forecasts.s: U.S.-China tariff truce extended again
forecasts.rs: Announcements by the White House or USTR and by China's Ministry of Commerce

forecasts.q: Prime Minister Takaichi and President Xi Jinping hold a China-Japan summit
forecasts.basis: China's economic retaliation is in its 11th month, and Takaichi has not retracted her remarks on a Taiwan contingency. The APEC meeting China hosts in November is the only opening.
forecasts.s: Takaichi-Xi summit
forecasts.rs: Announcements by the Japanese or Chinese foreign ministry (only a meeting that at least one of the two governments announces as a summit counts; a brief informal chat at the venue does not)

forecasts.q: Brent crude's final closing price of the year is below $90 a barrel
forecasts.basis: On top of the Hormuz blockade, the September shutdown of Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and its restart at reduced volumes have blocked supply routes twice over. If the forecast on a U.S.-Iran ceasefire and the reopening of Hormuz (f03) comes true, this one is likely to come true as well.
forecasts.s: Brent below $90 at year-end
forecasts.rs: The ICE Brent front-month futures (March 2027 contract) settlement price on December 31, 2026

forecasts.q: If a U.S.-North Korean summit takes place without South Korea formally taking part in the preparatory negotiations, the resulting agreement will contain no provisions on inter-Korean relations or on medium- and short-range missiles
forecasts.basis: Tests whether a U.S.-North Korean agreement becomes a deal covering only the threat to the U.S. homeland (ICBMs) · From the Korean Peninsula issue, Strategic Analysis tab
forecasts.s: No inter-Korean provisions in a U.S.-North Korean deal
forecasts.rs: The text of the U.S.-North Korea agreement (as released by the White House or KCNA)

forecasts.q: No inter-Korean military communication line is restored by December 31, 2026 (fails if South Korea's Ministry of National Defense or Ministry of Unification announces that regular calls with North Korea have resumed)
forecasts.basis: Baseline forecast assuming the current course (A0) holds. North Korea refuses any contact with the South, so the lines are unlikely to be restored in the two months or so that remain. · From the Korean Peninsula issue, Strategic Analysis tab
forecasts.s: Inter-Korean military lines not restored
forecasts.rs: Announcements by South Korea's Ministry of National Defense or Ministry of Unification

forecasts.q: No government-level (Red Cross) reunion of separated families, and no government-level exchange of confirmations on whether relatives are alive, resumes between the two Koreas by June 30, 2027 (fails if the Ministry of Unification announces a government-level reunion or exchange of such confirmations)
forecasts.basis: Baseline forecast assuming the current course (A0) holds. Government-level reunions and confirmations require North Korea's consent, and North Korea refuses any contact with the South. Private confirmations arranged through third countries do not count. · From the Korean Peninsula issue, Strategic Analysis tab
forecasts.s: Family reunions not resumed
forecasts.rs: Announcements by South Korea's Ministry of Unification

forecasts.q: China will not retaliate with open, large-scale economic measures, as it did over THAAD, against South Korea's pursuit of enrichment, reprocessing, and nuclear-powered submarines
forecasts.basis: Tests the assumption that the adversary responds in the most capable way · From the Korean Peninsula issue, Strategic Analysis tab
forecasts.s: No THAAD-style Chinese economic retaliation
forecasts.rs: Official announcements of measures by China's Ministry of Commerce or General Administration of Customs, and statements by the South Korean government

forecasts.q: By the end of 2028, inter-Korean family reunions or large-scale confirmations of whether relatives are alive take place at least once
forecasts.basis: A key sign of managed coexistence (F2) · From the 2030 futures in the Korean Peninsula issue, Strategic Analysis tab
forecasts.s: Family reunions by 2028
forecasts.rs: Announcements by South Korea's Ministry of Unification

forecasts.q: By the end of 2030, South Korea or Japan formalizes one of the following: a decision to develop nuclear weapons, withdrawal from the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT), or abandonment of its non-nuclear principles
forecasts.basis: The condition for nuclear dominoes (F3) · From the 2030 futures in the Korean Peninsula issue, Strategic Analysis tab
forecasts.s: South Korea or Japan formally goes nuclear
forecasts.rs: Official announcements by the South Korean or Japanese government, or a notice of withdrawal from the NPT

forecasts.q: By the end of 2030, North Korea's supreme leader changes, or an armed clash on the Korean Peninsula kills 100 or more people
