forecasts.q: By January 10, 2027, the United States and China again extend both the tariff truce and China's suspension of its rare-earth export controls, or replace them with a longer-term agreement
forecasts.basis: On September 24, 2026, the United States and China extended their tariff truce by two months and put off the core issues (tariffs, rare earths, and technology controls). The U.S. Russia sanctions law (the Graham Act), which took effect on September 18, mandates tariffs from October 18 on major buyers of Russian oil and gas and could have collided with the truce had China been targeted, but President Trump waived those tariffs on October 16. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the president would review the effects for up to 60 days · Grand strategy: AI concentrates value in a few hubs and turns those hubs into targets
forecasts.s: U.S.-China tariff truce and rare-earth pause extended
forecasts.rs: Announcements by the White House or USTR and by China's Ministry of Commerce

forecasts.q: By the end of 2027, the United States formally revokes its approval of H200-class AI chip exports to China, or lowers the approved volume through regulation, license conditions, or legislation (a de facto halt resulting from Chinese import restrictions or a company's production stoppage does not count)
forecasts.basis: Approval was announced in December 2025; the January 2026 rule capped volumes at 50 percent of U.S. domestic sales and collected a 25 percent levy in the form of a tariff; in May, licenses were granted to about 10 Chinese companies with a cap of 75,000 units per customer. China blocked imports, then allowed them on a limited basis from August (about 13 percent of the cap). A bill restricting the exports is pending in Congress. The current administration has tightened export controls when the trade truce was faltering and loosened them during truce periods (the H20 was re-approved three months after its 2025 ban), so the path most likely to lead to revocation is retaliation if the truce breaks down · The AI variable in the Taiwan Strait issue
forecasts.s: H200 exports to China revoked or cut
forecasts.rs: Rules or notices from the U.S. Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) or the text of legislation, or company disclosures or Reuters reporting

forecasts.q: By the end of 2027, North Korea states explicitly in its official media that it has applied AI or automation technology to the Nuclear Trigger (the state's comprehensive nuclear weapons management system) or to its nuclear counterattack command system
forecasts.basis: Announcements about delivery systems do not count (Kim Jong Un's February 2026 reference to AI in connection with the KN-25, which may have pointed to the production process, and May reports of an AI-guided cruise missile), nor does repetition of the law's wording that a strike is launched "automatically"; only an explicit statement that AI or automation technology has been applied to the command-and-control system counts. Nuclear powers have rarely stated officially that their nuclear command and control is technically automated (in 2011 the commander of Russia's Strategic Missile Forces confirmed that the Perimeter system exists and is on combat duty, but Moscow has never officially described how automated it is) · External variable X7 in the Korean Peninsula issue (shrinking human judgment and delegated authority)
forecasts.s: North Korea states AI use in nuclear command
forecasts.rs: KCNA and Rodong Sinmun reporting

forecasts.q: By the end of March 2027, a phased U.S.-Iran agreement (one that puts reopening the strait and lifting the blockade first and defers the nuclear issue to a later stage) is signed, and for at least 90 days after signing the strait stays open and the blockade stays lifted
forecasts.basis: Precedent: the U.S.-Iran memorandum of understanding of June 17, 2026, effectively collapsed three weeks later, on July 8 · Checked against prior attempts, Iran issue (C7)
forecasts.s: U.S.-Iran phased agreement holds 90 days

forecasts.s: China Coast Guard controls around Kinmen and Matsu

forecasts.q: By the end of June 2027, a major South Korean chipmaker officially announces a production cut or disruption due to a helium shortage, or such a disruption is reported by major media
forecasts.basis: Even while Qatar's helium production was halted for several months in 2026, no production disruptions at South Korean chipmakers were reported (thanks to inventories, recycling, and diversified sourcing). Qatari helium began shipping via Jeddah in August. Samsung Electronics and SK hynix hold four to six months of helium inventory. If this forecast comes true, it would signal that the assessment that a helium shortage amounts to no more than a cost burden was wrong · The AI variable in the Iran issue
forecasts.s: Helium shortage disrupts chip output
forecasts.rs: Company disclosures or statements, or major media reporting

forecasts.q: By January 31, 2027, a company or government announcement, or a report by Reuters, Bloomberg, or Yonhap, confirms that the United States has issued, for each of Samsung's Xi'an plant and SK hynix's Wuxi and Dalian plants, an equipment import license valid for at least six months of 2027 (annual licenses, multiyear licenses, and restoration of VEU status all count)
forecasts.basis: Equipment import licenses for 2026 were issued on December 30, 2025, one day before the plants' validated end-user (VEU) status expired, and TSMC's Nanjing plant (TSMC keeps only about 3 percent of its production capacity in China) received the same annual license. The U.S. administration does not want a memory supply shock. Whether the license conditions are tighter than those for 2026 will be noted separately. · AI and Chips issue
forecasts.s: U.S. licenses for Samsung and SK China plants
forecasts.rs: Company or government announcements, or reporting by Reuters, Bloomberg or Yonhap

forecasts.q: By December 31, 2026, the U.S. president signs a Section 232 proclamation that directly includes memory integrated circuits (HTS 8542.32) among the products subject to tariffs (resolves yes if they are among the covered products even with investment-linked exemptions or quotas attached; resolves no if only finished products containing memory are covered)
forecasts.basis: On September 2, 2026, the commerce secretary previewed a second phase of targeted tariffs on semiconductors, but no rates or timing have been announced, and the reported plans center on finished products containing chips. With three months left and the tariff truce extended, Washington also has little incentive to broaden tariffs. · AI and Chips issue
forecasts.s: Section 232 tariffs on memory chips
forecasts.rs: The proclamation and its annex product list as published in the Federal Register

forecasts.q: By June 30, 2027, Samsung Electronics or SK hynix announces a decision to build a memory wafer fab in the United States (excluding packaging and foundry) in a regulatory filing or press release that specifies the site or the investment amount (conditional reviews, memorandums of understanding, and reports that a plan is under consideration do not count)
forecasts.basis: On August 19, 2026, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources said South Korean companies had no plans to invest in memory production in the United States. Building a fab in the United States costs about twice as much as in South Korea and takes more than five years to reach operation. Yet the commerce secretary has demanded either a 100 percent tariff on memory or production in the United States. There is a precedent: after the 1993 U.S. antidumping duties on South Korean DRAM, South Korean makers built DRAM plants in the United States, but the announcements took two to three years, and it has not been established that the duties caused the plants to be built. · AI and Chips issue
forecasts.s: Samsung or SK decides on a U.S. memory fab
forecasts.rs: Samsung Electronics or SK hynix regulatory filings (DART) or press releases

forecasts.q: By June 30, 2027, China's Ministry of Commerce newly places a South Korean company, or a subsidiary at least 50 percent owned by a South Korean company, on the export control list, the Unreliable Entity List, the countermeasure list under the Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law, or a list under State Council Decree No. 835; or the suspension of sanctions on Hanwha Ocean's subsidiaries is not extended and the sanctions take effect again (excluded if the lapse is merely a technical gap and the suspension is renewed within 30 days)
forecasts.basis: Toward South Korea as a whole, China's default is to court it, but it readily imposes targeted sanctions on companies that cooperate with the United States (the October 2025 sanctions on Hanwha Ocean's subsidiaries). The suspension of the Hanwha Ocean sanctions ends on November 10, 2026, and it has not been confirmed whether it was extended along with the truce. Listings are also becoming more frequent, as with the addition of 10 U.S. companies in June 2026. · AI and Chips issue
forecasts.s: China lists South Korean companies
forecasts.rs: Notices by China's Ministry of Commerce

forecasts.q: As of January 15, 2027, Ministry of Commerce Announcements Nos. 55–58, 61, and 62 of 2025 (the October 2025 expansion of rare-earth export controls) remain suspended or have been withdrawn (as confirmed by a Ministry of Commerce announcement or a joint U.S.-China announcement)
forecasts.basis: The U.S.-China summit in September extended the tariff truce to January 10, 2027. China's rare-earth export controls deter most when held in reserve rather than actually used. Under the ministry's notices, however, the suspension expires on November 10, 2026, and no notice extending it has yet been confirmed. · AI and Chips issue
forecasts.s: China's rare-earth controls stay suspended
forecasts.rs: A Ministry of Commerce notice or a joint U.S.-China announcement

forecasts.basis: The Information reported on August 31, 2026, that CXMT had supplied HBM3E from risk production to Alibaba and Cambricon for testing. On the other hand, CXMT's HBM3 yields remain at 25 to 30 percent, and there are reports that CXMT's IPO prospectus includes no dedicated HBM business. The probability reflects the precedent of SMIC's 7nm chips, which were pushed into shipment with subsidies despite low yields. · AI and Chips issue

forecasts.rs: An official CXMT announcement, or reporting by at least two of Reuters, Bloomberg, TrendForce and DigiTimes

forecasts.q: In any quarter of 2027, CXMT's share of global DRAM revenue is reported at 15 percent or higher (by Counterpoint or TrendForce)
forecasts.basis: CXMT's share rose from 4 percent in the second quarter of 2025 to 10 percent in the second quarter of 2026 (9.5 percent according to TrendForce), and it is expanding capacity from 320,000 to 420,000 wafers a month. However, because the high unit price of HBM boosts South Korean makers' revenue, CXMT's gains in revenue share may lag its gains in output. · AI and Chips issue
forecasts.s: CXMT DRAM share at 15%
forecasts.rs: Counterpoint or TrendForce quarterly DRAM market reports

forecasts.q: By January 3, 2027 (the end of the 119th Congress), a law (a stand-alone bill or the National Defense Authorization Act) is enacted with the president's signature that contains at least one of the following: a provision banning sales of equipment and services to designated companies such as CXMT and YMTC, or a provision mandating U.S. extraterritorial controls if allies do not align by a deadline
forecasts.basis: The MATCH Act cleared the House Foreign Affairs Committee 44–0 (April 22, 2026) and is included in the manager's amendment to the Senate NDAA, but the Senate NDAA is stalled. The White House opposes having its discretion limited by statute, and there is a precedent: in 2025 the GAIN AI Act was dropped from the NDAA during final negotiations after industry lobbying. Whether an exemption for South Korean companies' plants in China is included will be noted separately. · AI and Chips issue

forecasts.q: The joint communiqué of the November 2026 Security Consultative Meeting (SCM) explicitly states that USFK will be maintained at 28,500 troops
forecasts.basis: The joint communiqués of 2019, 2021, 2023, and 2024 pledged to maintain U.S. forces in Korea at their "current level" without giving a number; the 2020 communiqué left the phrase out, and the 57th communiqué, in November 2025, dropped even the words "current level." The 2026 National Defense Strategy spells out South Korea's primary responsibility.
forecasts.s: SCM communiqué states USFK troop level
forecasts.rs: The text of the 2026 ROK-U.S. Security Consultative Meeting joint communiqué (as posted by the South Korean and U.S. defense ministries)

forecasts.q: By the end of 2030, the transfer of wartime operational control (OPCON) is completed and the Future Combined Forces Command is launched under a South Korean commander
forecasts.basis: South Korea has floated 2027–2028 and the USFK commander the first quarter of 2029, but the transfer has been postponed twice before. The U.S. National Defense Authorization Act barred spending on completing the transfer in a way that departs from the plan agreed by Seoul and Washington (fiscal 2026), and the Senate Armed Services Committee's bill would make completion of the transfer itself wait for the secretary of defense's certification and a 60-day waiting period.
forecasts.s: OPCON transfer completed by 2030
forecasts.rs: A joint announcement by the South Korean and U.S. defense ministries

forecasts.q: By the end of 2030, a reduction of USFK below 28,500 troops is confirmed by a U.S. government announcement or a report to Congress

forecasts.s: USFK falls below 28,500
forecasts.rs: A U.S. Department of Defense announcement or a report to the U.S. Congress

forecasts.q: By the end of 2030, the South Korean government formally pursues, through a government proposal or a bill, one of the following: extending active-duty service, introducing mandatory service for women, or switching to an all-volunteer force
forecasts.basis: The manpower gap is clear, but all three options carry very heavy political costs.
forecasts.s: Military service overhaul formally pursued
forecasts.rs: A government bill approved by the Cabinet, or a government-submitted bill in the National Assembly bill information system

forecasts.q: In the U.S. midterm elections on November 3, 2026, Democrats win at least 218 of the 435 House seats (based on each state's official results)
forecasts.s: Democrats win the House in the U.S. midterms
forecasts.basis: As of October 6, the Silver Bulletin's generic-ballot average gave Democrats an 8.9-point lead, and the Decision Desk HQ model (October 7) puts their chance of winning a House majority at 76 percent. The Cook Political Report (September 25) rates 208 seats as favoring Democrats, 205 as favoring Republicans, and 22 as toss-ups, so Democrats need to win only 10 of the 22 toss-ups for a majority. In the 20 midterm elections since 1946, the president's party gained House seats only twice, in 1998 and 2002. Redistricting in several states in 2025–2026, however, has added Republican-leaning districts, so Democrats' seat gains will not match their lead in the popular vote.
forecasts.rs: Official results certified by each state's election authority

forecasts.q: By February 28, 2027, Benjamin Netanyahu is prime minister of a new Israeli government that has won a Knesset vote of confidence (remaining prime minister of a caretaker government because no new government is formed does not count)
forecasts.s: Netanyahu returns as prime minister after Israel's election
forecasts.basis: In three early-October polls (Kan, September 28; Zman Yisrael, September 30–October 1; Channel 12, October 6), Netanyahu's coalition bloc won 49–53 seats, 8–12 short of a 61-seat majority. The opposition, too, has 49–54 seats without the Arab parties (12–13 seats), making a majority hard to reach on its own. In the 2022 election Netanyahu's bloc won 64 seats, about four more than the final polling average of 60.3, but this time it would have to overturn a larger gap. If neither side can form a government, as in 2019–2021, Netanyahu stays on as caretaker prime minister, but that outcome counts as a no for this forecast.
forecasts.rs: The Knesset's announcement of the confidence vote result

forecasts.q: By June 30, 2027, the U.S. or Polish government officially announces the location (city or base name) of a new permanent U.S. military base in Poland
forecasts.s: Location of a permanent U.S. base in Poland announced
forecasts.basis: Poland formally requested a new permanent base in June 2026. On September 17, President Trump said major progress had been made and that the location would be announced soon, and on September 22 President Nawrocki said the permanent base had been confirmed. On the other hand, the 2026 U.S. National Defense Strategy speaks of adjusting the U.S. force presence in Europe, and in May the United States canceled the deployment of an armored brigade to Poland.
forecasts.rs: An announcement by the U.S. Department of Defense or the Polish Ministry of National Defence

forecasts.q: By February 28, 2027, the Polish parliament passes the 2027 budget act, and the 2027 defense spending (the state budget and the Armed Forces Support Fund combined) published by the Ministry of Finance or the Ministry of National Defense immediately after passage is 4.5 percent of GDP or more
forecasts.s: Poland's 2027 defense spending set at 4.5% of GDP or more
forecasts.basis: The 2027 draft budget adopted by the Council of Ministers in late August 2026 puts defense spending at about 198.1 billion zlotys (4.51 percent of GDP), just above the threshold. The president signed the 2026 budget act on January 19 and referred it to the Constitutional Tribunal for follow-up review. Cuts during parliamentary deliberations or a revised GDP forecast could push the figure below 4.5 percent. At the first reading on October 8, 2026, Poland's lower house defeated a motion to reject the 2027 draft budget, 198 in favor and 237 against, and sent it to committee.
forecasts.rs: The Polish parliament's passage of the budget act and the defense spending figure published by Poland's Ministry of Finance or Ministry of National Defence

forecasts.q: By June 30, 2027, the government of a NATO member officially announces that a person has been killed on its territory, in its territorial waters, or in its airspace as a result of sabotage of military equipment or infrastructure carried out after October 10, 2026, by Russian or Belarusian state bodies (including proxies acting on their instructions), excluding targeted assassinations
forecasts.s: Deaths on NATO territory caused by Russia or Belarus
forecasts.basis: Prorating the 30 percent probability assigned to a deadly incident, then a patch-up (P2) through 2030 to a period of about nine months yields roughly 6 to 8 percent. The forecast is set at 12 percent after adding two further considerations: the rising frequency of incidents (the bombing of a railway line in November 2025, a missile crash in July 2026, and an explosives-laden drone at an airport in August) and the intelligence assessment disclosed by Prime Minister Tusk on September 17 that Russia is planning drone and missile attacks and that late autumn and winter will be the most dangerous period.
forecasts.rs: An official statement by the government of the NATO member concerned

forecasts.q: By December 31, 2026, Polish military authorities officially announce that a manned Russian or Belarusian military aircraft has again violated Polish airspace (only incidents after October 10, 2026, count)
forecasts.s: Russian or Belarusian manned aircraft violate Polish airspace again
forecasts.basis: On September 23, 2026, a Russian Mi-8 helicopter that had taken off from Kaliningrad flew about 300 meters into Polish airspace and stayed there for 42 seconds. It was the first publicly reported case of a Russian military helicopter crossing Poland's land border. The day before, Polish fighter jets intercepted a Russian Il-20 reconnaissance aircraft that had come close to the coast (outside Polish airspace).
forecasts.rs: An official statement by the Polish Armed Forces Operational Command or the Polish Ministry of National Defence

forecasts.q: By December 31, 2027, Germany's Ministry of Defense or the Bundeswehr officially announces that the 45th Panzer Brigade stationed in Lithuania has reached full operational readiness (volle Einsatzbereitschaft)
forecasts.s: German brigade in Lithuania reaches full readiness
forecasts.basis: The Bundeswehr plans to finish forming the brigade in the second half of 2027 and to bring it to full operational readiness, with at least 5,000 troops, before the end of 2027. A multinational battle group was folded into the brigade in February 2026. Even so, the creation of large units is often delayed by schedules for barracks and equipment.
forecasts.rs: An announcement by the German Ministry of Defence or the Bundeswehr

forecasts.q: By June 30, 2027, NATO or the U.S. government and Russia officially announce the restoration of a military-to-military hotline or an agreement to prevent accidental clashes covering Europe or the Baltic region
forecasts.s: NATO-Russia mechanism to prevent accidental clashes
forecasts.basis: The 2025 U.S. National Security Strategy lists reestablishing strategic stability with Russia among its priorities. In a diplomatic document reported by Reuters on September 30, 2026, however, Russia escalated its nuclear threats. Risk-reduction mechanisms are likely to be discussed together with a ceasefire in Ukraine.
forecasts.rs: Announcements by NATO, the U.S. government or the Russian Ministry of Defense

forecasts.q: By December 31, 2026, the Polish government requests consultations under Article 4 of the North Atlantic Treaty
forecasts.s: Poland requests NATO Article 4 consultations
forecasts.basis: Poland requested Article 4 consultations after the drone incursion of September 2025. No evidence could be found that it made such a request after the missile crash or the helicopter's violation of its airspace in 2026. A request is likely only after an incident in which people are killed.
forecasts.rs: An announcement by the Polish government or NATO

forecasts.q: By April 7, 2027, the U.S. Treasury extends General License 135 on Russian diesel or broadens it to cover Russian crude oil or other petroleum products
forecasts.s: Russian diesel license extended or broadened
forecasts.basis: Issued on October 9, 2026, the license runs through April 7, 2027. The announced diesel delivery schedule fits within that window, so an extension is not strictly needed, and in March 2025 the Treasury let General License 8L, which had allowed Russian energy-related payments, lapse. If dealings between Washington and Moscow widen, the license could be broadened to crude. This forecast tests Conclusion 5 of the Russia-Ukraine War analysis: that Russia's best move is to keep dealing with the United States.
forecasts.rs: OFAC's list of general licenses and its notices

forecasts.q: By March 31, 2027, the IAEA announces that it has verified on site the location and quantity of Iran's stockpile of 60 percent enriched uranium
forecasts.s: IAEA verifies Iran's 60% uranium stockpile on site
forecasts.basis: Since the war began, Iran has denied IAEA inspectors access to its facilities and says part of the stockpile is buried in rubble from the airstrikes. Even if a U.S.-Iran phased agreement is signed by the end of March (f38), verifying the stockpile is likely to come at a later stage. This forecast tests whether Washington's top-ranked course, phased negotiations with nuclear conditions (Conclusion 8), can be carried out.
forecasts.rs: Reports and statements by the IAEA director general

forecasts.q: By June 30, 2027, the IAEA or the government of a country involved announces that at least some of Iran's uranium enriched to 20 percent or more has been shipped out of Iran
forecasts.s: Iran's enriched uranium shipped abroad
forecasts.basis: On October 20, 2026, Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said that not a single gram of enriched uranium would be shipped out of Iran. In 2015, the shipment took place on December 28, five months after the nuclear deal was signed on July 14. This forecast tests whether Washington's opening demand in its top-ranked course, shipment to a third country, can be met (Conclusion 8).
forecasts.rs: Announcements by the IAEA and the U.S. and Iranian governments

forecasts.q: By February 28, 2027, the U.S. government formally announces the lifting or phased easing of its naval blockade of Iran
forecasts.s: U.S. lifts or eases naval blockade of Iran
forecasts.basis: Lifting the blockade is one of the terms that would go into the first phase of a U.S.-Iran agreement. The estimate is set in line with the forecasts of a ceasefire and reopening of the strait by year's end (f03, 20 percent) and of a phased agreement signed by the end of March (f38, 25 percent). This forecast tests whether Washington moves from staying the course to a phased agreement (Conclusions 8 and 9).
forecasts.rs: Announcements by the White House, the Pentagon and U.S. Central Command

forecasts.q: By March 31, 2027, the U.S. Senate passes, in a floor vote, a war powers resolution restricting the president's military action against Iran
forecasts.s: Senate passage of an Iran war powers resolution
forecasts.basis: A war powers resolution failed in the Senate, 49–50, on September 24, 2026, with one senator not voting. Four Republicans voted yes, among them Sen. Thom Tillis, who leaves the Senate in early 2027. The outcome depends heavily on the Senate seats decided in the November 3 midterm elections. The forecast is a signal for the external variable 'Congress restrains the war' and tests how much weight the U.S. goal of limiting costs and sharing burdens carries.
forecasts.rs: U.S. congressional records (congress.gov)

forecasts.q: In Taiwan's November 28, 2026, local elections, Kuomintang nominees or joint candidates formally endorsed by the Kuomintang and the Taiwan People's Party win at least 12 of the 22 mayoral and county magistrate posts (independents and candidates backed by the Taiwan People's Party alone do not count)
forecasts.s: Kuomintang wins 12+ of Taiwan's 22 mayoral and county races
forecasts.basis: The Kuomintang holds 13 or 14 of the 22 posts, so the question is whether it loses two or fewer. The party is running a joint candidate with the Taiwan People's Party for mayor of New Taipei, but the two parties ended their cooperation in Hsinchu County on September 6. The outcome would be an early signal of a Kuomintang victory in the 2028 presidential election (an external variable, 45 percent) and would prompt a fresh look at the odds of a U.S.-China bargain over Taiwan (brokered stability).
forecasts.rs: Certified results from Taiwan's Central Election Commission

forecasts.q: By December 31, 2026, European Council conclusions (including those of the special summit on November 26–27 and the December summit) approve a new, named funding instrument with a stated euro amount for Ukraine's 2027 financing needs, separate from the €90 billion loan already approved
forecasts.s: EU approves new 2027 funding for Ukraine
forecasts.basis: At their October summit, EU leaders asked the European Commission to find roughly €70 billion for Ukraine in 2027, and they will take up the question alongside the next long-term budget at a special summit on November 26–27. Hungary's April 2026 election eased the obstacles to unanimity. Still, writing an amount and an instrument into the conclusions is a high bar, and the €90 billion loan was not agreed until December 2025. A yes would be a signal against a pullback in European support (an external variable, 30 percent).
forecasts.rs: European Council conclusions

forecasts.q: On at least one day from November 1, 2026, through March 31, 2027, the settlement price of the front-month Dutch TTF natural gas contract (not the intraday price) exceeds €100 per megawatt-hour
forecasts.s: European gas tops €100 per megawatt-hour
forecasts.basis: On October 9, EU gas storage was 73.5 percent full, 16.9 percentage points below the five-year average, and disruptions to Qatari LNG supplies are continuing. If stocks drain faster during the January–February peak in winter demand, prices are likely to break €100. The forecast tracks how the Iran war is feeding into European households' heating bills and consumer prices.
forecasts.rs: ICE Endex settlement prices (or settlement prices reported by Reuters if ICE data are not accessible)

forecasts.q: From November 1, 2026, through January 31, 2027, attacks halt flows through Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline or crude loadings at the port of Yanbu for at least seven consecutive days, or attacks cut daily merchant transits of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait below 10 ships for seven consecutive days
forecasts.s: Saudi pipeline or Red Sea shipping halted for a week or more
forecasts.basis: The Houthis, who declared a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia on July 22, have since attacked Saudi tankers and energy facilities. Strikes on pipeline pumping stations stopped flows for 11 days, September 11–22. With the Strait of Hormuz closed, Saudi crude exports are concentrated at Yanbu, so losing this bypass would cause Gulf crude exports to collapse.
forecasts.rs: Announcements by Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry and Aramco, and ship-tracking counts from Windward and in Reuters reports

forecasts.q: By December 31, 2026, Germany's Bundestag passes a 2027 federal budget that allocates more than the €11.6 billion in the government's draft for military support to Ukraine (resolves no if the budget is not passed by year-end)
forecasts.s: Germany increases Ukraine aid in its 2027 budget
forecasts.basis: On July 6, the German cabinet approved a 2027 budget draft with €11.6 billion for military support to Ukraine, and the Bundestag is scheduled to hold its final vote in November. For the 2026 budget, the Bundestag added about €3 billion in Ukraine support during its deliberations. In 2027, however, sharply higher defense spending and heavy new borrowing leave little room for an increase. With U.S. aid reduced, the outcome will show whether Europe's largest donor to Ukraine increases its support further.
forecasts.rs: Records of the adopted budget from Germany's Federal Ministry of Finance and the Bundestag (the comparison uses total military support to Ukraine counted on the same basis as the €11.6 billion in the government's draft)

forecasts.q: By January 31, 2027 (Korea time), the joint communiqué of the 58th Security Consultative Meeting (SCM) commits to keeping U.S. Forces Korea (USFK) at 28,500 troops or at its "current level" (resolves no if no communiqué is published by then)
forecasts.s: 58th SCM communiqué commits to current USFK level
forecasts.basis: A commitment to keep USFK at its current level appeared in the joint communiqués of the 51st SCM in 2019, the 53rd in 2021 and the 56th in 2024, but was missing from the 52nd in 2020. The 57th communiqué, in November 2025, said only that USFK "will maintain force and posture levels," without the word "current." In the fiscal 2026 National Defense Authorization Act, Congress barred the Pentagon from spending money to cut USFK below 28,500 troops unless it justifies the reduction to Congress. The 2026 National Defense Strategy, by contrast, assigns South Korea primary responsibility for deterring North Korea. This year's meeting is reported likely to slip to around December over disagreements on the conditions for transferring wartime operational control (OPCON). Unlike the site's earlier forecast, which assumes a November meeting, this one asks only what the communiqué says, whenever the meeting is held, as long as the communiqué is published by January 31, 2027.
forecasts.rs: The text of the 58th SCM joint communiqué, as posted by South Korea's Ministry of National Defense or the U.S. Department of Defense, in either Korean or English. It must commit to keeping USFK troops or forces at their "current level" (including wording such as "current USFK force levels") or at 28,500. Wording like the 57th communiqué's "will maintain force and posture levels," which gives neither the current level nor a number, does not count, nor does a mention of the 28,500 figure that is not a commitment.

forecasts.q: By June 30, 2027, North Korea conducts a flight test of an intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM); ground tests of engines or motors and satellite launches do not count
forecasts.s: North Korea resumes ICBM flight tests
forecasts.basis: North Korea has not flight-tested an ICBM since the Hwasong-19 on October 31, 2024. Development has continued, however, with a ground test of a solid-fuel engine in September 2025, the unveiling of the Hwasong-20 at a military parade in October 2025, and a solid-fuel motor test in March 2026. The pauses in ICBM flight testing have coincided with periods of U.S.-North Korean summit diplomacy, in 2018–2019 and again since 2025. The probability rises if a Trump-Kim meeting falls through.
forecasts.rs: An announcement by South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff or Japan's Ministry of Defense that a launch was ICBM-class, or a Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) announcement of an ICBM test

forecasts.q: By June 30, 2027, North Korean state media announce an ICBM test moratorium and link it to talks or an agreement with the United States
forecasts.s: North Korea ties an ICBM test moratorium to talks with Washington
forecasts.basis: In April 2018 North Korea declared a halt to nuclear and ICBM tests and went on to the Singapore summit in June. On September 21, 2025, Kim Jong Un said he could talk with the United States if Washington dropped its demand for denuclearization, but would not bargain anything away in exchange for sanctions relief. Whether Pyongyang puts a moratorium publicly on the table will show what it wants in return.
forecasts.rs: A KCNA or Rodong Sinmun statement, or a joint U.S.-North Korean document, that includes language on a moratorium on ICBM (or strategic weapons) tests

thinkers.name: Thucydides
thinkers.works: History of the Peloponnesian War (an unfinished history that runs from the outbreak of war in 431 BCE and breaks off in 411; eight books in its present form)
thinkers.bio: An Athenian whose dates of birth and death are estimates. He states that when war broke out in 431 BCE he began his record at once, expecting it to be a great war (1.1). He wrote that he lived through the entire 27-year war old enough to understand events and took pains to learn the facts accurately (5.26.5). The following year, in 430 BCE, he caught the plague and survived, and he recorded its symptoms from his own illness and from watching other patients (2.48.3). As a general, he lost Amphipolis to the Spartan Brasidas in the winter of 424 BCE and spent 20 years in exile, which, by his own account, allowed him to spend time with both sides, especially the Peloponnesians, and to observe events more closely (5.26.5).
thinkers.claim: He divided the causes of the war into the reasons openly given and what he called the truest cause. The disputes over Corcyra and Potidaea were the reasons given; the truest cause was the growth of Athenian power and the fear it aroused in Sparta (1.23.6). This is why he is called the founder of realism. Yet the maxim that the strong do what they can and the weak suffer what they must belongs to the Athenian envoys who demanded the surrender of Melos in 416 BCE; it is not his own conclusion (5.89). Directly after his account of the execution of the adult men of Melos and the sale of its women and children into slavery (5.116), he narrates how Athens was crushed in the Sicilian expedition (415–413 BCE). He also wrote that after the plague neither fear of the gods nor law held anyone back (2.53), and that war is a rough teacher that brings people's characters down to the level of their circumstances (3.82). He recorded the damage war does even to individual health and to the community.
thinkers.develop: He set out his method in 1.22. Speeches were kept as close as possible to the general sense of what was actually said, while the speakers were made to say what each situation demanded; events were established by rigorous cross-checking of eyewitness accounts; and the work was written as a possession for all time, not a piece for the applause of the moment, for readers who want to understand a future that, human affairs being what they are, will resemble the past. He argued that even the Peace of Nicias, concluded in 421 BCE, could not be counted as peace, and treated the 27 years as a single war (5.26). In 1629 Thomas Hobbes published the first English translation made directly from the Greek; in the 20th century, realists such as Hans Morgenthau and E. H. Carr drew on him; and Graham Allison derived the concept of the "Thucydides Trap" from 1.23.6.
thinkers.critique: In The Outbreak of the Peloponnesian War (1969), Donald Kagan examined the major decision points one by one and rejected the diagnosis in 1.23.6, arguing that the war could have been avoided at several junctures and grew out of choices made by Corinthian, Spartan, and Athenian leaders. Malcolm Heath argued in 1986 that fear did less to trigger the war directly than to make Athenian conduct appear unjust. In The Tragic Vision of Politics (2003), Richard Ned Lebow held that Thucydides the realist is only the surface of the narrative, beneath which lies the lesson that the language of power ultimately destroys the strong themselves. As for Allison, Arthur Waldron objected in 2017 that no such trap appears in the original text and that Kagan and Ernst Badian had already overturned the proposition. In a 2020 book, Steve Chan criticized Allison's account as overly structural, and in a scholarly symposium on that book, Yuan-kang Wang pointed out that it was Sparta, the established power, that started the Peloponnesian War.
thinkers.now: The Allison entry in the list of reference thinkers interprets the reciprocal visits of the U.S. and Chinese leaders in 2026 and the tariff truce extended to January 2027 as efforts to manage the relationship so as to avoid the Thucydides Trap. In Thucydides's terms, tariffs and arms sales to Taiwan are the reasons given; the shift in power and the fear beneath them do not disappear with a summit. Clisa Geopolitics places a commitment formalizing South Korean military participation in a Taiwan contingency at the bottom of its ranking, citing in support the case of Athens, which made only a defensive alliance with Corcyra yet was drawn into the fighting anyway (1.44–55). In the Russia-Ukraine war, the Easter, Victory Day, and early-September ceasefires all ended in renewed fighting, and the site, pointing to the Peace of Nicias, judges that a ceasefire without guarantees, an outcome it puts at 18 percent, may be only one phase of a war of attrition.
thinkers.record: Where he has been borne out: a Harvard Belfer Center case study that generalizes his diagnosis of the Peloponnesian War in 1.23.6, made in the late fifth century BCE, found that 12 of the 16 cases since the late 15th century in which a rising power confronted an established one ended in war. His observation that those who survived the plague of 430 BCE either did not catch it again or did not die if they did (2.51.6) is regarded as an early record of acquired immunity. Where he has fallen short: in the same study, four cases, including the United States and the Soviet Union during the Cold War and the United Kingdom and France with Germany from the 1990s onward, passed without war. As for the Peloponnesian War itself, Kagan in 1969 saw it as an avoidable war, and Wang pointed out in 2020 that the side that opened it was the established power. These criticisms converge on the view that shifts in power and fear create the conditions for war, while whether war actually begins depends on leaders' choices.

props.t: In wars between great powers, the fear that a rising power's growth arouses in the established power tends to be a deeper cause than the disputes openly put forward.
A lull produced by a peace treaty may not be peace but a phase of the same war.
War is a rough teacher that brings most people's characters down to the level of their circumstances.

quote.ko: "For the truest cause, though the least evident in what was said, was, I believe, that the Athenians, by growing great and causing fear among the Lacedaemonians [Spartans], compelled them to go to war."
quote.orig: τὴν μὲν γὰρ ἀληθεστάτην πρόφασιν, ἀφανεστάτην δὲ λόγῳ, τοὺς Ἀθηναίους ἡγοῦμαι μεγάλους γιγνομένους καὶ φόβον παρέχοντας τοῖς Λακεδαιμονίοις ἀναγκάσαι ἐς τὸ πολεμεῖν
quote.src: Thucydides, History of the Peloponnesian War 1.23.6. Greek text from the Oxford edition edited by H. Stuart Jones (1910), checked against the passage as quoted in Parmeggiani's article (Mnemosyne 71, 2018). English translation by Clisa Geopolitics

thinkers.name: Plato
thinkers.works: Apology, Republic, Statesman, Laws, Seventh Letter (authenticity disputed). Laws is a work of his last years.
thinkers.bio: Born in Athens in 428/427 BCE, he studied under Socrates and died in 348/347. By his own account in the Seventh Letter (whose authenticity is disputed), he meant as a young man to enter public life, but although the Thirty, the oligarchy installed in 404 BCE, invited him to take part, he drew back when the regime tried to involve Socrates in its arrests and executions of citizens. When the restored democracy executed Socrates in 399 BCE, he writes, he concluded that every city was badly governed and that the ills of cities would not cease unless philosophers ruled. He founded the Academy in Athens in the 380s BCE, and according to the letter, after a first visit to Syracuse at about age 40, he went back around 366 and around 361 BCE to try to educate Dionysius II.
thinkers.claim: In the Republic, Socrates says that the ills of cities will not cease unless philosophers become kings or kings take up philosophy. This is the archetype of the question of rule by expertise. Books 8 and 9 explain how the best city decays in turn into timocracy, oligarchy, democracy, and tyranny. Change begins with division within the ruling group (545d); excessive freedom turns into excessive servitude and gives rise to tyranny (564a); and the tyrant keeps stirring up wars so that the people will need a leader (566e) and holds on to power only by getting rid of the brave and the wise (567b–c). In Book 1 of the Laws, it is the Cretan Clinias who says that peace is only a name, and the Athenian who leads the dialogue counters that legislation should aim at peace, not war. Plato set the happiness of the whole city, not of a single class (420b), as the purpose of politics; in that respect his starting point differs from that of Clisa Geopolitics, which takes the capabilities of individual human beings as its purpose.
thinkers.develop: The ideal city of the Republic presupposed philosopher-rulers and a guardian class holding property and families in common. In the Laws, a late work, the emphasis shifts to law. In Book 9, the Athenian says that a ruler with absolute power who answers to no one will, because of human nature, end up pursuing private interest, and that since people so outstanding that they need no law are now scarcely to be found anywhere, the second-best course of law and order must be chosen (875a–d). Book 3 holds that a good city must combine elements of monarchy and democracy.
thinkers.critique: In Book 2 of the Politics, Aristotle objected that a city that becomes too much of a unity is no longer a city, that what is common to the greatest number receives the least care, and that having the same people always rule breeds strife. He also rejected the goal of the happiness of the whole city, arguing that the whole cannot be happy unless most of its parts are. In The Spell of Plato, the first volume of The Open Society and Its Enemies (1945), Karl Popper characterized Plato's design as a totalitarian project, and in an April 1988 article in The Economist, he summed up his position: instead of asking who should rule, one should ask how to avoid situations in which bad rulers can do great harm. Ronald Levinson challenged this reading in In Defense of Plato (1953).
thinkers.now: The Power Structures tab of Clisa Geopolitics describes North Korea as a system of one-man rule by the general secretary, who is also chairman of the State Affairs Commission, and Russia as a system in which authority is concentrated in the president. In Iran, Mojtaba Khamenei succeeded his late father as supreme leader in March 2026, and in China, the purges of Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli left only two of the seven members of the Central Military Commission in place, concentrating decision-making even further in the hands of President Xi Jinping. In countries like these, war and negotiation hinge on the judgment of a few. In the Republic, Plato hoped that such judgment would be wise; in the Laws, he distrusted unchecked rulers and chose law.
thinkers.record: Where he has fallen short: his visits to Syracuse around 366 and around 361 BCE, which put rule by philosophers to the test, failed. According to the Seventh Letter, he went to teach Dionysius II for fear of seeming a man of mere words, but Dion was driven into exile by slander, and Plato himself barely got away on his third visit. Dion later seized power and was assassinated. Against the scheme in which regimes degenerate in a fixed order, Aristotle cited counterexamples in Book 5, Chapter 12 of the Politics, in which oligarchy turned into tyranny and one tyranny into another. Where he has been borne out: the proposition in Republic 545d, that a regime does not change as long as its ruling group holds together, points in the same direction as the 1986 conclusion of Guillermo O'Donnell and Philippe Schmitter that no transition has begun without important divisions within the regime itself. Barbara Geddes, however, argued in 2004 that splits lead to collapse mainly in military regimes, and that in one-man dictatorships, which suppress factions, splits become dangerous only when compounded by events such as the leader's serious illness.

props.t: Regime change begins with a split in the ruling group, and as long as the ruling group holds together, the regime does not change.
A tyrant keeps stirring up wars so that the people will need a leader.
Since in reality there is no ruler so outstanding as to need no law, the rule of law, the second-best option, should be chosen over unchecked power.

quote.ko: "Unless either philosophers become kings in the cities, or those now called kings and potentates genuinely and adequately pursue philosophy, so that political power and philosophy coincide in one, while the many natures that now pursue either one apart from the other are forcibly excluded, there is no rest from ills, my dear Glaucon, for the cities, nor, I think, for the human race."
quote.orig: ἐὰν μή, ἦν δʼ ἐγώ, ἢ οἱ φιλόσοφοι βασιλεύσωσιν ἐν ταῖς πόλεσιν ἢ οἱ βασιλῆς τε νῦν λεγόμενοι καὶ δυνάσται φιλοσοφήσωσι γνησίως τε καὶ ἱκανῶς, καὶ τοῦτο εἰς ταὐτὸν συμπέσῃ, δύναμίς τε πολιτικὴ καὶ φιλοσοφία, τῶν δὲ νῦν πορευομένων χωρὶς ἐφʼ ἑκάτερον αἱ πολλαὶ φύσεις ἐξ ἀνάγκης ἀποκλεισθῶσιν, οὐκ ἔστι κακῶν παῦλα, ὦ φίλε Γλαύκων, ταῖς πόλεσι, δοκῶ δʼ οὐδὲ τῷ ἀνθρωπίνῳ γένει
quote.src: Plato, Republic 5.473c–d. Socrates speaks these words to Glaucon in setting out the claim he likens to the greatest of the waves. Greek text from Burnet's Oxford edition (1903). English translation by Clisa Geopolitics

thinkers.name: Aristotle
thinkers.works: Nicomachean Ethics, Politics, Metaphysics, Poetics (dates of composition unknown)
thinkers.bio: Born in 384 BCE in Stagira, near the Macedonian border, he died in Chalcis in 322 BCE. He entered Plato's Academy in Athens in 367 BCE, at about 17, and stayed some 20 years, until Plato's death in 348/347 BCE. He then spent about three years at Assos in Asia Minor and about two years on the island of Lesbos, and from 343 BCE he tutored the 13-year-old Macedonian prince Alexander. He returned to Athens in 335 BCE and founded the Lyceum; after Alexander died in 323 BCE, he was charged with impiety amid anti-Macedonian sentiment and left Athens for Chalcis.
thinkers.claim: Book 1, Chapter 7 of the Nicomachean Ethics defines the human good (happiness, or eudaimonia) as activity of the soul in accordance with virtue, carried on over a complete life (1098a16–18). Happiness, in other words, is not a feeling but a life lived exercising one's capacities well. The Politics holds that the state (polis) exists for the sake of living well and is not merely an alliance to prevent injustice (Book 3, Chapter 9). It distinguishes kingship, aristocracy, and polity from their corrupt forms of tyranny, oligarchy, and democracy, according to whether one, a few, or many rule, and whether they rule for the common interest or for themselves (Book 3, Chapter 7). He held that a state with a large middle class is likely to be well governed (Book 4, Chapter 11) and that inequality is everywhere the cause of revolution (Book 5). In her 1988 paper "Nature, Function, and Capability," Martha Nussbaum argued that Amartya Sen is at one with Aristotle in valuing goods by the human functioning they make possible, and she built the capabilities approach on Aristotle.
thinkers.develop: Unlike Plato, who designed an ideal state, he collected and compared actual states. The list of his works preserved by Diogenes Laertius includes a book setting out the constitutions of 158 states. Book 7 of the Politics places a limit on the size of the state, on the grounds that citizens must know one another's characters to judge lawsuits and distribute offices properly.
thinkers.critique: In Book 1 of the Politics, he held that some people are slaves by nature and that slavery is beneficial and just for them (Chapter 5), and that women possess the capacity to deliberate but lack authority (Chapter 13). In Chapter 15 of Leviathan (1651), Thomas Hobbes rejected this doctrine of natural slavery as contrary to both reason and experience, and in Chapter 11 he wrote that there is no greatest good of the kind the old moral philosophers spoke of, and that happiness is an endless progress of desire from one object to the next.
thinkers.now: Clisa Geopolitics takes the happiness of individual human beings as its final end but does not define happiness itself; instead, it measures capabilities, the conditions for pursuing the life each person considers good, across the seven categories of human security defined by the UN. Unlike Aristotle, who also laid out what a good life consists of, it measures only the conditions. Clisa Geopolitics also distinguishes regime survival from people's lives, which follows the same line as his distinction between rule for the common interest and rule for the ruler's own sake. On Iran, too, it sums up the Iranian government's yardstick as regime survival, while recommending, from the standpoint of individual lives, that humanitarian aid for the Iranian people be raised through diplomatic channels as well.
thinkers.record: Where he has been borne out: Seymour Martin Lipset, acknowledging Aristotle's influence, argued in 1959 that a middle class enlarged by economic development sustains democracy, in line with the proposition in Book 4, Chapter 11 of the Politics that a country with a large middle class is likely to be well governed; and Adam Przeworski and Fernando Limongi showed in 1997, using data on 135 countries from 1950 to 1990, that the richer a country, the more stable its democracy. Where he has fallen short: in the same study, economic development did not raise the probability of a transition to democracy, and Andrew Nathan reported in 2016 that China's middle class supports the authoritarian regime even as it embraces liberal values. His thinking on the size of the state also missed the mark. Though he tutored Alexander, he theorized only the polis, and after his death in 322 BCE most Greek poleis lost any real independence under the successor kingdoms.

props.t: A country with a large middle class is likely to be well governed.
Inequality is everywhere the cause of revolution.
The state exists for the sake of living well, and rule for the ruler's own benefit rather than the common interest is a corrupt form of government.

quote.ko: "The complete community formed from several villages is the state, which has reached, so to speak, the limit of full self-sufficiency; it comes into being for the sake of life, but it exists for the sake of the good life. … From these things, then, it is evident that the state belongs among the things that exist by nature, and that man is by nature a political animal."
quote.orig: ἡ δ᾿ ἐκ πλειόνων κωμῶν κοινωνία τέλειος πόλις, ἤδη πάσης ἔχουσα πέρας τῆς αὐταρκείας ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν, γινομένη μὲν τοῦ ζῆν ἕνεκεν, οὖσα δὲ τοῦ εὖ ζῆν. … ἐκ τούτων οὖν φανερὸν ὅτι τῶν φύσει ἡ πόλις ἐστί, καὶ ὅτι ὁ ἄνθρωπος φύσει πολιτικὸν ζῷον
quote.src: Aristotle, Politics 1.2, 1252b27–30, 1253a1–3. A claim the author advances in his own voice in explaining the origin of the state. English translation by Clisa Geopolitics

It distinguishes kingship, aristocracy, and polity from their corrupt forms of tyranny, oligarchy, and democracy, according to whether one, a few, or many rule, and whether they rule for the common interest or for themselves (Book 3, Chapter 7). He held that a state with a large middle class is likely to be well governed (Book 4, Chapter 11) and that inequality is everywhere the cause of revolution (Book 5). In her 1988 paper "Nature, Function, and Capability," Martha Nussbaum argued that Amartya Sen is at one with Aristotle in valuing goods by the human functioning they make possible, and she built the capabilities approach on Aristotle.

thinkers.name: Immanuel Kant
thinkers.role: Philosopher, professor at the University of Königsberg
thinkers.works: Critique of Pure Reason (1781), "Idea for a Universal History with a Cosmopolitan Aim" (1784), Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals (1785), Toward Perpetual Peace (1795), The Metaphysics of Morals (1797)
thinkers.bio: Born on April 22, 1724, in Königsberg, Prussia (now Kaliningrad, Russia), he died in the same city on February 12, 1804. He entered the University of Königsberg in 1740 and studied under Martin Knutzen; around 1748 he left without a degree and worked for about six years as a private tutor, then in 1755 obtained his master's degree and the right to lecture and began teaching at his old university. He became a full professor in 1770, at 46, and his major works, including the Critique of Pure Reason (1781), all came after that. "Idea for a Universal History" appeared in the Berlinische Monatsschrift in November 1784, and Toward Perpetual Peace was published in Königsberg by Nicolovius in 1795.
thinkers.claim: Of the six preliminary articles in Toward Perpetual Peace, Kant classed three as laws to be observed immediately: the first, that a peace treaty concluded with a secret reservation of grounds for a future war is merely a truce; the fifth, that no state should forcibly interfere in the constitution and government of another; and the sixth, which forbids, even in wartime, hostilities that would make mutual trust impossible in a future peace. The three definitive articles are a republican constitution, a federation of free states, and a cosmopolitan right limited to universal hospitality. By a republic he meant not democracy but a system that separates legislative from executive power. The federation is not a world state but a league of peace without coercive power, what he called a negative surrogate, offered because states reject a world republic. Cosmopolitan right is a right to visit, not a right to take possession, and in the same passage he condemned European colonial conquest. Underlying all of this is the categorical imperative to treat people never merely as means but always at the same time as ends, a formulation also quoted in the philosophy questions section of Clisa Geopolitics.
thinkers.develop: In the 1784 "Idea for a Universal History," he argued that the tendency of human beings to seek one another's company while resisting one another, which he called unsocial sociability, drives people into a society governed by law, and that war, too, pushes states toward a league of nations in which even the smallest state is defended by united power. In Toward Perpetual Peace, he held that the spirit of commerce, which cannot coexist with war, leads states to promote peace not out of morality but out of self-interest, and counted it among the guarantees of peace that nature provides.
thinkers.critique: In the remark to Section 333 of the Philosophy of Right (1820), Hegel objected that because there is no judge above states, a league rests on particular sovereign wills and cannot escape contingency; in Section 334, he wrote that when those wills cannot be reconciled, only war can settle the matter. Sebastian Rosato countered in the American Political Science Review in 2003 that democracies, too, distrust one another when their interests collide, and that it is uncertain whether peace among democracies is owed to democracy. In The Great Delusion (2018), John Mearsheimer argues that liberal hegemony, which seeks to spread democracy abroad, brought on, among other things, conflict with Russia over NATO enlargement. Clisa Geopolitics has likewise noted that because Kant's articles take trust between states as their standard, human rights such as ordinary people's access to information fall outside that framework.
thinkers.now: On the Korean Peninsula, Clisa Geopolitics invokes the sixth preliminary article in judging that information operations aimed at North Korea that come close to inciting regime overthrow are something Seoul should restrain on its own rather than hold in reserve as a bargaining chip. In the Russia-Ukraine war, the short ceasefires at Easter, on Victory Day, and in early September all ended in renewed fighting, and Clisa Geopolitics puts the probability of a Minsk-style ceasefire without guarantees from great-power troops at 18 percent. This is the same diagnosis as the first article: a treaty that leaves the seeds of a future war is merely a truce. Under a literal reading of the fifth article, the U.S. military's capture of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro in January amounts to prohibited forcible interference. On the Taiwan Strait, the finding that Congress has offset or delayed the U.S. administration's deals with China through the Taiwan Relations Act and other means echoes Kant's view of the separation of powers as the core of a republic. NATO, a party to the Russia-NATO standoff, is a collective defense alliance against external threats, so its purpose differs from that of Kant's league of peace, which aims to end war among its own members.
thinkers.record: Where he has been borne out: on Kant's 1795 view that republics would hesitate to go to war, Michael Doyle reported in Philosophy & Public Affairs in 1983 that constitutionally secure liberal states had not fought one another for almost 200 years, and explained this through Kant's three definitive articles. John Oneal and Bruce Russett, using data from 1885 to 1992, reported that democracy, economic interdependence, and membership in international organizations lower the likelihood of armed conflict (Triangulating Peace, 2001). Where he has fallen short: Doyle himself noted that liberal states are not peaceful toward nonliberal ones, pointing out that the advance to the Yalu River in the Korean War and the Vietnam War instead deepened the adversaries' dependence on the Soviet Union. Among the covert interventions he left out of his analysis, those aimed at elected governments, such as Árbenz's in Guatemala and Allende's in Chile, point to a remaining problem: democratic peace theory looks only at open war. Whether to treat the 1999 Kargil conflict between India and Pakistan as an exception also depends on how democracy is defined.

props.t: Republics, in which the decision to go to war requires the consent of the citizens, are very hesitant to start a war.
The spirit of commerce, which cannot coexist with war, sooner or later takes hold of every people and leads states to promote peace not out of morality but out of self-interest.
People must never be treated merely as means but always at the same time as ends.

quote.ko: "If (as cannot be otherwise under this constitution) the consent of the citizens is required to decide 'whether there shall be war or not,' then nothing is more natural than that, since they would have to decide to bring all the hardships of war upon themselves (such as doing the fighting themselves, paying the costs of the war out of their own property, painfully repairing the devastation it leaves behind ...), they will think very hard before beginning so bad a game."
quote.orig: Wenn (wie es in dieser Verfassung nicht anders sein kann) die Beistimmung der Staatsbürger dazu erfordert wird, um zu beschließen, »ob Krieg sein solle, oder nicht«, so ist nichts natürlicher, als daß, da sie alle Drangsale des Krieges über sich selbst beschließen müßten (als da sind: selbst zu fechten; die Kosten des Krieges aus ihrer eigenen Habe herzugeben; die Verwüstung, die er hinter sich läßt, kümmerlich zu verbessern; ...), sie sich sehr bedenken werden, ein so schlimmes Spiel anzufangen
quote.src: Immanuel Kant, Zum ewigen Frieden. Ein philosophischer Entwurf (Königsberg: Friedrich Nicolovius, 1795), Second Section, First Definitive Article, AA VIII 351. English translation by Clisa Geopolitics

thinkers.name: Halford Mackinder
thinkers.works: "The Geographical Pivot of History" (1904), Democratic Ideals and Reality (1919), "The Round World and the Winning of the Peace" (1943)
thinkers.bio: Born in Gainsborough, Lincolnshire, in February 1861, he died in 1947. He entered Christ Church, Oxford, in 1880 and studied zoology under Henry Moseley, the naturalist of the Challenger expedition, before switching to modern history; he later recalled that he did so to see how the theory of evolution worked itself out in human development. From 1885 he worked as a traveling lecturer in the university extension movement, and in 1887, the year he published "On the Scope and Methods of Geography," he took up Oxford's first post in geography, a readership, which he held until 1905. He served as principal of Reading College (1892–1903), director of the London School of Economics, or LSE (1903–1908), and member of Parliament (1910–1922), and he presented the 1904 pivot paper while serving as both reader at Oxford and director of the LSE. In late 1919, as British high commissioner for South Russia, he was charged with uniting the White forces.
thinkers.claim: In a lecture to the Royal Geographical Society on January 25, 1904, Mackinder argued that the "Columbian epoch," the 400 years in which a sea-dominant Western Europe had encircled Eurasia from outside, had ended around 1900. The pivot region is the interior of Eurasia, inaccessible to ships but open in earlier ages to mounted nomads. What he saw first in the railway was military mobility. A state at the center of the continent that moved troops and supplies by rail along short internal routes could concentrate its strength ahead of a sea power that had to take the long way around by sea, a logic known as the advantage of interior lines. His evidence was the Russian railway running 6,000 miles from the western frontier to Vladivostok and the Russian army in Manchuria. His warning was that if this pivot state expanded to the margins of Eurasia and used the continent's resources to build a fleet, world empire would be within sight, and he named an alliance between Germany and Russia as the event that could set this in motion.
thinkers.develop: In Democratic Ideals and Reality (1919), he renamed the pivot region the Heartland and extended it to the basins of the Baltic and the Black Sea. Viewing World War I as a struggle between Germans and Slavs over Eastern Europe, he wrote that the statesmen at the peace conference should keep in mind the saying "Who rules East Europe commands the Heartland: Who rules the Heartland commands the World-Island: Who rules the World-Island commands the World," the World-Island being Eurasia and Africa. His prescription was a tier of independent states, including Poland, between Germany and Russia to serve as a buffer zone. In a July 1943 article in Foreign Affairs, he judged that if the Soviet Union defeated Germany, it would become the greatest land power on the globe, and he proposed that an Atlantic power, binding the North Atlantic together as a "Midland Ocean" and using Britain as "a moated aerodrome," join with the Soviet Heartland to encircle Germany from both sides.
thinkers.critique: In the Russo-Japanese War, which began on February 8, 1904, two weeks after the lecture, Russian reinforcements were slowed because the railway section around Lake Baikal was unfinished, and Russia was defeated in 1905. Since Mackinder himself had acknowledged the fragility of the single-track line, this was less a refutation than a condition that the technology of the day placed on the theory. In the discussion after the lecture, Leo Amery pointed out that air power would be added to the sea and the railway, and that the nations with the greatest industrial base would prevail. In 1944, Nicholas Spykman argued that the scheme of land power against sea power was wrong, since in the Napoleonic Wars and both world wars Britain and Russia had instead stood together against a strong power on the coastal rim. Critics also point to the use of his concepts as a rationale for territorial expansion in Karl Haushofer's German Geopolitik and, as Gerry Kearns (2009) noted, to the way they made the pursuit of empire look like a duty of great powers.
thinkers.now: The Russia-Ukraine war is a fight over what Mackinder called Eastern Europe: the western gateway into the Heartland. Continued attrition is rated the most likely future through 2030, at 36 percent. A war of attrition now in its fifth year shows that even a Heartland state cannot easily take control of Eastern Europe. In 1919, Mackinder described the Baltic as, strategically, a closed sea of the Heartland, but since Finland (2023) and Sweden (2024) joined NATO, the Baltic has become a sea ringed mostly by NATO members. Over Kaliningrad, the Russian territory on its shores, Russia warned NATO on September 30 that if the exclave were blockaded, it could use all weapons, including nuclear weapons.
thinkers.record: The German-Russian alliance that he named in 1904 as the event that could lead to world empire came closest to reality with the German-Soviet Nonaggression Pact of August 1939, but it did not last two years: Germany invaded the Soviet Union in June 1941. His 1919 proposition that whoever rules East Europe commands the Heartland seemed to hold when the Soviet Union, having taken control of Eastern Europe after World War II, became a superpower facing the United States, but the Soviet Union, too, dissolved in December 1991 without ever ruling the World-Island. The North Atlantic framework he proposed in 1943 became reality six years later with the founding of NATO in April 1949, but the Soviet Union, which he had meant to include, became the adversary NATO was built to contain. The tier of buffer states in Eastern Europe that he prescribed in 1919, by contrast, collapsed with the German and Soviet invasions of Poland in September 1939. The interior's advantage, which he traced in 1904 to its inaccessibility to ships, diminished sharply with the arrival of aircraft, missiles, and nuclear weapons, as Amery had anticipated that same year.

props.t: If a continental power in the Eurasian interior gains mobility through railways, expands to the periphery, and builds a fleet with the continent's resources, it draws closer to world empire.
Because whoever rules Eastern Europe commands the Heartland, the fate of Eastern Europe decides the contest for continental hegemony.
A tier of independent states should be established between Germany and Russia so that no single continental power can hold both Eastern Europe and the Heartland.

quote.ko: "The Russian army in Manchuria is as significant evidence of mobile land-power as the British army in South Africa was of sea-power. True, that the Trans-Siberian railway is still a single and precarious line of communication, but the century will not be old before all Asia is covered with railways."

thinkers.name: Nicholas Spykman
thinkers.role: American scholar of international politics, professor at Yale University
thinkers.works: America's Strategy in World Politics (1942), The Geography of the Peace (1944, published posthumously), "Geography and Foreign Policy" (1938)
thinkers.bio: Spykman was born in Amsterdam in October 1893 and died in New Haven, Connecticut, in June 1943. He studied at Delft and at the University of Cairo, and from 1913 to 1920 worked as a journalist in the Near East, Java (then part of the Dutch East Indies), and the Middle East. In 1920 he moved to the University of California, Berkeley, where he earned his doctorate in 1923 with a study of Georg Simmel. He joined Yale in 1925, and in 1935 became chair of its Department of International Relations and the founding director of the Yale Institute of International Studies. His geopolitics began as a policy argument against isolationism and the doctrine of hemisphere defense, both gaining ground in the United States in the late 1930s: the United States, he contended, had to involve itself in the balance of power in Eurasia.
thinkers.claim: Spykman accepted Mackinder's map but reversed his conclusion. Because the Heartland has little arable land and is ringed by ice and high mountains that make transport difficult, he reasoned that Soviet power would remain west of the Urals unless the resources of Central Asia proved comparable to those of the rimland. The decisive zone was the rimland, the belt between the Heartland and the surrounding seas that runs from the European coastland through Arabia and the Middle East to the monsoon lands of India and East Asia. The rimland was an amphibious zone that had to defend itself on both land and sea, and a vast buffer zone where land power and sea power collided. The core of U.S. security, he argued, was therefore to keep the rimlands at both ends of Eurasia from falling to a single hostile power or coalition; if that happened, the United States would be encircled regardless of the size of its army and navy. The United States had gone to war twice in 30 years, he explained, because Germany and Japan had sought to dominate the Eurasian coastlands.
thinkers.develop: In America's Strategy in World Politics, published in March 1942, he rebutted the case for hemisphere defense. Geography, he argued, is the most fundamental factor in foreign policy because it is the most permanent; in international anarchy the aim of foreign policy is to preserve a state's relative power position, and values such as justice and fairness can be considered only insofar as they do not interfere with that aim. In the same book he wrote that "a Russian state from the Urals to the North Sea can be no great improvement over a German state from the North Sea to the Urals," argued that German and Japanese military power need not be eliminated after the war, and predicted that China, not Japan, would be the main postwar problem in East Asia. The rimland concept was systematized only after his death in June 1943, in The Geography of the Peace (1944), compiled from his lectures of fall 1942.
thinkers.critique: Reviewing the book in Political Science Quarterly in March 1943, Edward Mead Earle objected to its narrow conception of power as the sole foundation of international politics and to its exaggeration of strategic geography, countering that technology can alter geography. He warned that a prescription of setting Germany against Russia and China against Japan could become a policy that loses both the shirt and the soul. When Life called Spykman an advocate of cold-blooded power politics in December 1942, he replied in a January 1943 letter that he had also proposed regional leagues of nations, and argued that collective security works only when power is roughly in balance. Because his theory was completed before nuclear weapons appeared, it could not address how nuclear deterrence changes the meaning of geography.
thinkers.now: Most of today's major flashpoints (the Black Sea, the Strait of Hormuz, India and Pakistan, the South China Sea, the Taiwan Strait, and the Korean Peninsula) lie along the rimland belt. Because the rimland is so vast, however, this alone does not prove him right. In 1942 Spykman foresaw that "a modern, vitalized, and militarized China of 400 million people" would threaten the position of the Western powers in the "Asiatic Mediterranean" (the South China Sea and the waters of Southeast Asia), and that Chinese air power might one day control that sea. The chance that China will be reported by the end of November to have again blocked resupply of Second Thomas Shoal is put at 30 percent. His prescription was to use allies in the rimland as a foothold, yet the United States, while extending its tariff truce with China to January 2027, has unilaterally scaled back its combined exercises with South Korea and imposed Section 301 tariffs on its allies. Greenland, where the United States signed a security agreement with Denmark in September, is one of the places where, Spykman wrote in 1944, the United States should base naval and air forces.
thinkers.record: In America's Strategy in World Politics (1942), he held that Germany and Japan could remain pillars of the balance of power after the war; Japan became a U.S. ally through the U.S.-Japan Security Treaty of September 1951, and West Germany through its accession to NATO in May 1955. His forecast in the same book that China, not Japan, would be the main problem in East Asia came true with the founding of the People's Republic of China in October 1949 and China's intervention in the Korean War in October 1950. The rimland logic is regarded as the geographic prototype of Cold War containment, earning him the nickname "godfather of containment." In 1944, by contrast, he judged that as long as the Soviet Union did not seek hegemony over the European rimland, it would be the most effective continental base for keeping the peace, and that cooperation among the United States, Britain, and the Soviet Union would be the foundation of postwar security. That cooperation gave way to the Cold War in March 1947, when the United States proclaimed the Truman Doctrine to stop Soviet expansion.

props.t: Whoever controls the rimland along the Eurasian coast rules Eurasia, and whoever rules Eurasia controls the destinies of the world.
The United States should engage in the balance of power to keep the rimlands at both ends of Eurasia from falling to a single hostile power or coalition.
A modernized and militarized China threatens the Western position in the South China Sea and the waters of Southeast Asia.

quote.ko: "Who controls the rimland rules Eurasia; who rules Eurasia controls the destinies of the world."
